title.zh: 卷四百七十三 列傳第二百三十二 姦臣三 黃潛善 汪伯彥 秦檜
title.en: Volume 473 Biographies 232: Treacherous Officials 3 - Huang Qianshan, Wang Boyan, Qin Hui
title.raw: 卷四百七十三 列傳第二百三十二 姦臣三 黃潛善 汪伯彥 秦檜 Volume 473 Biographies 232: Treacherous Officials 3 - Huang Qianshan, Wang Boyan, Qin Hui

sentences.zh: 黃潛善 汪伯彥 秦檜

translations.literal: Huang Qianshan, Wang Boyan, Qin Hui.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Qianshan, Wang Boyan, and Qin Hui.

sentences.zh: 黃潛善

translations.literal: Huang Qianshan.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Qianshan.

sentences.zh: 黃潛善，字茂和，邵武人。

translations.literal: Huang Qianshan, style name Maohe, was a native of Shaowu.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Qianshan, whose style name was Maohe, came from Shaowu.

sentences.zh: 擢進士第，宣和初，為左司郎。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination. At the beginning of the Xuanhe reign, he served as Left Department Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: After passing the jinshi examination, he was appointed Left Department Gentleman at the start of the Xuanhe era.

sentences.zh: 陝西、河東地大震，陵谷易處，徽宗命潛善察訪陝西，因往視。

translations.literal: A great earthquake struck Shaanxi and Hedong; hills and valleys changed place. Emperor Huizong ordered Qianshan to inspect Shaanxi, and he went to look.
translations.idiomatic: When a major earthquake struck Shaanxi and Hedong, shifting hills and valleys from their places, Emperor Huizong ordered Qianshan to investigate Shaanxi, and he went to see for himself.

sentences.zh: 潛善歸，不以實聞，但言震而已。

translations.literal: When Qianshan returned, he did not report the facts, but spoke only of the earthquake.
translations.idiomatic: On his return, Qianshan failed to report what he had actually found and mentioned only that there had been an earthquake.

sentences.zh: 擢戶部侍郎，坐事謫亳州，以徽猷閣待制知河間府。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Vice Minister of Revenue, then demoted to Bozhou for an offense, and later appointed Prefect of Hejian as Huaiyou Pavilion Attendant-Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to Vice Minister of Revenue, he was later demoted to Bozhou for an offense, then appointed Prefect of Hejian with the title of Huaiyou Pavilion Attendant-Drafter.

sentences.zh: 靖康初，金人入攻，康王開大元帥府，檄潛善將兵入援。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Jingkang era, when the Jurchens invaded, the Prince of Kang opened the Grand Marshal's headquarters and summoned Qianshan to lead troops in relief.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jingkang era, as the Jurchens invaded, the Prince of Kang established the Grand Marshal's headquarters and ordered Qianshan to march with troops to the capital's aid.

sentences.zh: 張邦昌僭位，潛善趨白于帥府，王承制拜潛善為副元帥。

translations.literal: When Zhang Bangchang usurped the throne, Qianshan hurried to report it to the marshal's headquarters. The Prince, acting under emergency authority, appointed Qianshan deputy marshal.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Bangchang seized the throne, Qianshan rushed to inform the marshal's headquarters, and the Prince, exercising emergency authority, appointed him deputy marshal.

sentences.zh: 明年，金人攻陝西，京東、山東盜起，潛善、伯彥匿不以聞。

translations.literal: The next year, when the Jurchens attacked Shaanxi and bandits rose in Jingdong and Shandong, Qianshan and Boyan concealed the news and did not report it.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, as the Jurchens attacked Shaanxi and bandits rose across Jingdong and Shandong, Qianshan and Boyan suppressed the reports and never informed the court.

sentences.zh: 張遇焚真州，距行在六十里，內侍邵成章疏潛善、伯彥誤國，成章坐除名。

translations.literal: Zhang Yu burned Zhenzhou, sixty li from the temporary capital. Eunuch Shao Chengzhang memorialized that Qianshan and Boyan had harmed the state. Chengzhang was dismissed from office for it.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Yu burned Zhenzhou, only sixty li from the temporary capital, eunuch Shao Chengzhang submitted a memorial accusing Qianshan and Boyan of ruining the country—and was himself stripped of office for his trouble.

sentences.zh: 御史馬伸亦以劾潛善、伯彥得罪，謫監濮州酒稅，道卒。

translations.literal: Censor Ma Shen also offended by impeaching Qianshan and Boyan. He was demoted to supervise wine taxes at Puzhou and died on the road.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Ma Shen likewise fell afoul of the court for impeaching Qianshan and Boyan; he was demoted to supervise wine taxes at Puzhou and died en route.

sentences.zh: 潛善進左僕射兼門下侍郎。

translations.literal: Qianshan was promoted to Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and concurrent Vice Director of the Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: Qianshan was promoted to Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, concurrently serving as Vice Director of the Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 鄆、濮相繼陷沒，宿、泗屢警，右丞許景衡以扈衛單弱，請帝避其鋒，潛善以為不足慮，率同列聽浮屠克勤說法。

translations.literal: Yan and Pu fell in succession; Suzhou and Sizhou were repeatedly alarmed. Right Vice Director Xu Jingheng, noting the weakness of the imperial guard, asked the emperor to avoid the enemy's edge. Qianshan thought it not worth worrying about and led his colleagues to hear the Buddhist monk Keqin preach.
translations.idiomatic: As Yan and Pu fell one after another and Suzhou and Sizhou came under repeated threat, Right Vice Director Xu Jingheng, seeing how thin the imperial guard was, urged the emperor to withdraw from the enemy's path. Qianshan dismissed the concern and led his fellow ministers to listen to the Buddhist monk Keqin preach.

sentences.zh: 俄泗州奏金人且至，帝大驚，決策南渡。

translations.literal: Soon Sizhou reported that the Jurchens were about to arrive. The emperor was greatly alarmed and decided to cross south.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Sizhou reported that the Jurchens were approaching, and the emperor, deeply alarmed, resolved to flee south across the Yangtze.

sentences.zh: 禦舟已戒，潛善、伯彥方共食，堂吏大呼曰：「駕行矣。」

translations.literal: The imperial boat was already prepared. Qianshan and Boyan were just eating together when a clerk shouted loudly: "The imperial procession is departing!"
translations.idiomatic: The imperial boat was already made ready, yet Qianshan and Boyan were still at table together when a clerk cried out, "The emperor is leaving!"

sentences.zh: 乃相視蒼黃鞭馬南馳。

translations.literal: They looked at each other in panic and whipped their horses south in flight.
translations.idiomatic: They exchanged panicked glances and whipped their horses south in desperate flight.

sentences.zh: 都人爭門而出，死者相枕藉，人無不怨憤。

translations.literal: The people of the capital scrambled for the gates to get out; the dead lay piled upon one another. Everyone was filled with resentment and rage.
translations.idiomatic: The people of the capital surged through the gates in a stampede, corpses heaped upon corpses, and none escaped bitterness and fury.

sentences.zh: 會司農卿黃鍔至江上，軍士聞其姓以為潛善也，爭數其罪，揮刃而前，鍔方辯其非是，而首已斷矣。

translations.literal: When Minister of Revenue Huang E arrived on the river, soldiers hearing his surname thought he was Qianshan. They competed to recite his crimes and rushed forward with blades drawn. E had just begun to protest that they were mistaken when his head was already severed.
translations.idiomatic: When Minister of Revenue Huang E reached the river, soldiers who heard his surname took him for Qianshan, clamored to list his crimes, and rushed forward with drawn blades. E had barely begun to protest his identity when his head was already off.

sentences.zh: 帝渡瓜州，幸鎮江，敵兵已躡其後。

translations.literal: The emperor crossed at Guazhou and proceeded to Zhenjiang. Enemy troops were already pressing close behind.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor crossed at Guazhou and made for Zhenjiang, with enemy troops already close on his heels.

sentences.zh: 潛善、伯彥聯疏言艱難之時，不敢具文求退。

translations.literal: Qianshan and Boyan submitted a joint memorial saying that in these difficult times they dared not present a formal request to retire.
translations.idiomatic: Qianshan and Boyan submitted a joint memorial saying that in such dire times they dared not file a formal request to resign.

sentences.zh: 中丞張澄劾之，乃罷潛善為觀文殿大學士、知江寧府，落職居衡州。

translations.literal: Censor-in-Chief Zhang Cheng impeached them. Qianshan was then dismissed and made Grand Academician of the Hall for Viewing Literature and Prefect of Jiangning, then stripped of office and sent to live at Hengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Censor-in-Chief Zhang Cheng impeached them, Qianshan was removed from office, given the nominal title of Grand Academician of the Hall for Viewing Literature and appointment as Prefect of Jiangning, then stripped of rank and exiled to Hengzhou.

sentences.zh: 鄭瑴又論潛善、伯彥均于誤國，而潛善之惡居多，王庭秀繼以為言，責置英州。

translations.literal: Zheng Yue further argued that Qianshan and Boyan were equally guilty of harming the state, but Qianshan's evil was the greater. Wang Tingxiu followed with the same charge, and Qianshan was punished by assignment to Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Yue argued further that Qianshan and Boyan were equally responsible for the ruin of the state, though Qianshan's crimes were the greater; Wang Tingxiu added his voice, and Qianshan was banished to Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 諫官袁植乞斬之都市，帝不許。

translations.literal: Remonstrance official Yuan Zhi asked that he be executed in the capital market. The emperor did not consent.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrance official Yuan Zhi petitioned for Qianshan's public execution in the capital, but the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 尋卒于梅州。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he died at Meizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He soon died at Meizhou.

sentences.zh: 潛善猥持國柄，嫉害忠良。

translations.literal: Qianshan basely held the reins of state and envied and harmed the loyal and worthy.
translations.idiomatic: Qianshan shamelessly wielded state power, envying and destroying loyal and worthy men.

sentences.zh: 李綱既逐，張愨、宗澤、許景衡輩相繼貶死，憲諫一言，隨陷其禍，中外為之切齒。

translations.literal: After Li Gang was driven out, Zhang Xie, Zong Ze, Xu Jingheng, and others were demoted and died in succession. A single word from a censor or remonstrator would at once bring ruin, and both inside and outside the court gnashed their teeth over it.
translations.idiomatic: After Li Gang was driven from office, Zhang Xie, Zong Ze, Xu Jingheng, and others were demoted and died in turn; a single word from any censor or remonstrator would bring immediate ruin, and men throughout the court and country ground their teeth in fury.

sentences.zh: 高宗末年有旨，潛善、余深、薛昂皆復官錄後。

translations.literal: In the late years of Emperor Gaozong there was an edict restoring the offices of Qianshan, Yu Shen, and Xue Ang and enfeoffing their descendants.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of Emperor Gaozong's reign, an edict restored the official ranks of Qianshan, Yu Shen, and Xue Ang and granted posthumous honors to their heirs.

sentences.zh: 諫官淩哲言深、昂朋附蔡京，潛善專恣誤國，今盡復三人恩數，恐政刑失平，忠義解體。

translations.literal: Remonstrance official Ling Zhe said that Shen and Ang had attached themselves to Cai Jing, and Qianshan had acted arbitrarily and harmed the state. To restore all three to favor now, he feared, would unbalance law and governance and dissolve the bonds of loyalty and righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrance official Ling Zhe argued that Shen and Ang had been partisans of Cai Jing and Qianshan had acted with reckless arrogance to ruin the country; restoring all three to favor, he warned, would throw law and governance out of balance and unravel the fabric of loyalty and righteousness.

sentences.zh: 詔以潛善嘗任副元帥，特復元官，錄一子。

translations.literal: An edict stated that because Qianshan had once served as deputy marshal, his original office alone was specially restored and one son was enfeoffed.
translations.idiomatic: An edict held that because Qianshan had once served as deputy marshal, his original rank alone would be restored and one son granted posthumous honors.

sentences.zh: 汪伯彥

translations.literal: Wang Boyan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Boyan.

sentences.zh: 汪伯彥，字廷俊，徽之祁門人。

translations.literal: Wang Boyan, style name Tingjun, was a native of Qimen in Huizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Boyan, whose style name was Tingjun, came from Qimen in Huizhou.

sentences.zh: 登進士第，積官為虞部郎官。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination and rose through offices to become a Gentleman of the Bureau of Parks and Forests.
translations.idiomatic: After passing the jinshi examination, he rose through the ranks to become a Gentleman of the Bureau of Parks and Forests.

sentences.zh: 靖康改元，召見，獻河北邊防十策，直龍圖閣、知相州。

translations.literal: When the reign title changed to Jingkang, he was summoned for an audience and presented ten strategies for the northern frontier. He was made Directly Attached to the Dragon Diagram Hall and Prefect of Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jingkang era began, he was summoned to court, presented ten strategies for defending the northern frontier, and was appointed Directly Attached to the Dragon Diagram Hall and Prefect of Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 是冬，金人陷真定，詔徙真定帥司於相，俾伯彥領之。

translations.literal: That winter, when the Jurchens took Zhending, an edict moved the Zhending command headquarters to Xiang and had Boyan lead it.
translations.idiomatic: That winter, after the Jurchens captured Zhending, an edict transferred the Zhending military command to Xiangzhou and placed Boyan in charge.

sentences.zh: 高宗以康王使金至磁，時金騎充斥，嘗有甲馬數百至城下，蹤跡王所在。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Kang, later Emperor Gaozong, went as envoy to the Jurchens and reached Ci, Jurchen cavalry filled the countryside. Once several hundred armored horsemen came to the city walls tracking the Prince's whereabouts.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Kang, later Emperor Gaozong, was sent as envoy to the Jurchens and reached Ci, Jurchen cavalry swarmed the region; on one occasion several hundred armored riders came to the city walls searching for the Prince.

sentences.zh: 伯彥亟以帛書請王還相，躬服橐鞬，部兵逆王於河上。

translations.literal: Boyan urgently sent a letter on silk asking the Prince to return to Xiang, personally donned armor, and led troops to meet the Prince on the river.
translations.idiomatic: Boyan urgently sent a letter urging the Prince to return to Xiangzhou, donned armor himself, and led troops to meet him on the river.

sentences.zh: 王勞之曰：「他日見上，當首以京兆薦公。」

translations.literal: The Prince thanked him, saying: "When I see the emperor another day, I shall first recommend you for Jingzhao."
translations.idiomatic: The Prince thanked him, saying, "When I next see the emperor, I shall recommend you first for the post at Jingzhao."

sentences.zh: 其受知自此始矣。

translations.literal: His gaining favor began from this.
translations.idiomatic: From this moment his favor with the Prince began.

sentences.zh: 未幾，王奉蠟書，開天下兵馬大元帥府，以伯彥為副將。

translations.literal: Before long the Prince received the sealed edict and opened the Grand Marshal's headquarters for all armies and horses, appointing Boyan deputy commander.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the Prince received the sealed imperial edict, established the Grand Marshal's headquarters for all armies, and appointed Boyan his deputy commander.

sentences.zh: 王引兵渡河，謀所向，言人人殊，伯彥獨曰：「非出北門濟子城不可。」

translations.literal: The Prince led troops across the river and deliberated where to go. Each man spoke differently, but Boyan alone said: "We cannot do otherwise than leave by the north gate and cross at Zicheng."
translations.idiomatic: The Prince led his troops across the river and debated their next move; opinions differed widely, but Boyan alone insisted, "We must leave by the north gate and cross at Zicheng—there is no other way."

sentences.zh: 王喜曰：「廷俊言是也。」

translations.literal: The Prince was pleased and said: "Tingjun is right."
translations.idiomatic: The Prince was pleased and said, "Tingjun is right."

sentences.zh: 既濟，由大名曆鄆、濟達于南京，奏為集英殿修撰。

translations.literal: After crossing, they passed through Daming, Yan, and Ji to reach Nanjing. Boyan was memorialized for appointment as Compiler in the Hall for Gathering Excellence.
translations.idiomatic: After crossing, they traveled through Daming, Yan, and Ji to Nanjing, and Boyan was recommended for appointment as Compiler in the Hall for Gathering Excellence.

sentences.zh: 北兵薄京城，欽宗詔：金人見議通和，康王將兵，毋得輕動。

translations.literal: Northern troops pressed close to the capital. Emperor Qinzong edicted: "The Jurchens are now discussing peace. The Prince of Kang is leading troops—do not act rashly."
translations.idiomatic: As northern troops closed on the capital, Emperor Qinzong issued an edict: "The Jurchens are now negotiating peace; the Prince of Kang holds the army—do not move rashly."

sentences.zh: 伯彥以為然。

translations.literal: Boyan thought this correct.
translations.idiomatic: Boyan agreed.

sentences.zh: 宗澤曰：「女真狂譎，是欲款我師爾。

translations.literal: Zong Ze said: "The Jurchens are wild and cunning. They only wish to stall our army.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Ze said, "The Jurchens are wild and deceitful—they only mean to stall our army.

sentences.zh: 如即信之，後悔何及乎！

translations.literal: If we believe them at once, how can we regret it in time!
translations.idiomatic: If we trust them now, what regret will come too late!

sentences.zh: 宜亟進兵。」

translations.literal: We should advance the army at once."
translations.idiomatic: We should advance immediately."

sentences.zh: 伯彥等難之。

translations.literal: Boyan and the others objected.
translations.idiomatic: Boyan and the others objected.

sentences.zh: 及城破，金人逼二帝北行，張邦昌僭立，王聞之涕泣。

translations.literal: When the city fell, the Jurchens forced the two emperors north. Zhang Bangchang usurped the throne. When the Prince heard it he wept.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell and the Jurchens marched the two emperors north, Zhang Bangchang seized the throne—and the Prince wept at the news.

sentences.zh: 明年春，王承制除伯彥顯謨閣待制，升元帥，進直學士。

translations.literal: The next spring the Prince, acting under emergency authority, appointed Boyan Xianmo Pavilion Attendant-Drafter, promoted him to marshal, and advanced him to Direct Academician.
translations.idiomatic: The following spring the Prince, exercising emergency authority, appointed Boyan Xianmo Pavilion Attendant-Drafter, promoted him to marshal, and made him Direct Academician.

sentences.zh: 高宗即位，擢知樞密院事。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozong took the throne, Boyan was promoted to Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozong ascended the throne, Boyan was promoted to Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 未幾，拜右僕射。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was appointed Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 方高宗初政，天下望治。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Gaozong's rule, the whole realm hoped for good government.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Gaozong's reign, the whole realm looked for good government.

sentences.zh: 伯彥、潛善逾年在相位，專權自恣，不能有所經畫。

translations.literal: Boyan and Qianshan held the chief ministership for more than a year, monopolizing power as they pleased and accomplishing nothing of substance.
translations.idiomatic: Boyan and Qianshan held the chief ministership for more than a year, wielding power as they pleased and achieving nothing of substance.

sentences.zh: 御史諫官，下至韋布內侍，皆劾奏之。

translations.literal: From censors and remonstrators down to commoners and eunuchs, all impeached and memorialized against them.
translations.idiomatic: Censors and remonstrators, commoners and eunuchs alike, all impeached and memorialized against them.

sentences.zh: 罷伯彥為觀文殿大學士、知洪州，改提舉崇福宮，尋落職居永州。

translations.literal: Boyan was dismissed and made Grand Academician of the Hall for Viewing Literature and Prefect of Hongzhou, then changed to Director of the Chongfu Palace, and soon stripped of office and sent to live at Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Boyan was removed from office, given the nominal title of Grand Academician of the Hall for Viewing Literature and appointment as Prefect of Hongzhou, then reassigned to direct the Chongfu Palace, and soon stripped of rank and exiled to Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 紹興初，復職，知池州、江東安撫大使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Shaoxing era his office was restored and he was made Prefect of Chizhou and Grand Pacification Commissioner of Jiangdong.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Shaoxing era his rank was restored and he was appointed Prefect of Chizhou and Grand Pacification Commissioner of Jiangdong.

sentences.zh: 言者弗置，乃詔以舊職奉祠，尋知廣州。

translations.literal: Critics would not let the matter rest, so an edict had him serve in his old rank as a temple commissioner. Soon he was made Prefect of Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Critics would not let the matter drop, so an edict assigned him to a temple commission at his former rank; he was soon made Prefect of Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 四年，帝追贈陳東、歐陽澈。

translations.literal: In the fourth year the emperor posthumously honored Chen Dong and Ouyang Che.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year the emperor posthumously honored Chen Dong and Ouyang Che.

sentences.zh: 舍人王居正論伯彥、潛善不已，復褫前職。

translations.literal: Drafting official Wang Juzheng continued to denounce Boyan and Qianshan without cease, and Boyan's former office was again stripped.
translations.idiomatic: Drafting official Wang Juzheng kept denouncing Boyan and Qianshan without letup, and Boyan's restored rank was stripped once again.

sentences.zh: 七年，帝謂輔臣曰：「元帥舊僚，往往淪謝，惟汪伯彥實同艱難。

translations.literal: In the seventh year the emperor said to his chief ministers: "The old companions of the marshal's headquarters have mostly passed away. Only Wang Boyan truly shared the hardships.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year the emperor told his chief ministers, "The old companions from the marshal's headquarters have mostly passed away; only Wang Boyan truly shared those hardships.

sentences.zh: 朕之故人，所存無幾，宜與牽復。」

translations.literal: Of my old friends, few remain. He should be restored."
translations.idiomatic: Of my old friends, few remain—I should see him restored."

sentences.zh: 秦檜、張浚曰：「臣等已議曰郊恩取旨，更得天筆明其舊勞，庶幾內外孚信。」

translations.literal: Qin Hui and Zhang Jun said: "We have already discussed taking instruction on the suburban grace amnesty. If we further receive the emperor's own brush to clarify his old service, perhaps inside and outside will be equally convinced."
translations.idiomatic: Qin Hui and Zhang Jun said, "We have already discussed handling this through the suburban grace amnesty; if Your Majesty's own brush further clarifies his past service, court and country alike may be persuaded."

sentences.zh: 始伯彥之未第也，受館于王氏，檜嘗從之學，而浚亦伯彥所引，故共贊焉。

translations.literal: Earlier, before Boyan passed the examinations, he had tutored in the Wang household, and Hui had once studied under him. Jun too had been recommended by Boyan. Therefore they jointly supported him.
translations.idiomatic: In earlier days, before Boyan had passed the examinations, he had tutored in the Wang household—Hui had been among his pupils—and Jun too had been recommended by Boyan; so they joined in supporting his restoration.

sentences.zh: 九年，知宣州，過闕，帝謂檜曰：「伯彥便令之官，庶免紛紜。」

translations.literal: In the ninth year, as Prefect of Xuanzhou, he passed through the capital. The emperor said to Hui: "Let Boyan proceed directly to his post, so as to avoid turmoil."
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year, while serving as Prefect of Xuanzhou, he passed through the capital; the emperor told Hui, "Let Boyan proceed directly to his post, so as to avoid controversy."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「伯彥潛藩舊僚，去國七年。

translations.literal: He also said: "Boyan is an old companion from the prince's domain. He has been away from court for seven years.
translations.idiomatic: He added, "Boyan is an old companion from my days as prince; he has been away from court for seven years.

sentences.zh: 漢之高、光不忘豐沛、南陽故舊，皆人情之常。」

translations.literal: Gaozu and Guangwu of Han did not forget their old companions of Feng and Pei, and of Nanyang. This is the common way of human feeling."
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu and Guangwu of Han never forgot their old companions from Feng and Pei, and from Nanyang—that is only human nature."

sentences.zh: 伯彥上所著《中興日曆》五卷，拜檢校少傅、保信軍節度使。

translations.literal: Boyan submitted his five-juan work, Calendar of the Restoration, and was appointed Honorary Junior Tutor and Military Commissioner of Baoxin.
translations.idiomatic: Boyan submitted his five-juan work, Calendar of the Restoration, and was appointed Honorary Junior Tutor and Military Commissioner of Baoxin.

sentences.zh: 十年，請祠，從之。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he requested a temple commission and was granted it.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he requested a temple commission and the request was granted.

sentences.zh: 明年五月，卒，贈少師，諡忠定。

translations.literal: The next year, in the fifth month, he died. He was posthumously made Junior Preceptor and given the posthumous title Zhongding.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, in the fifth month, he died; he was posthumously made Junior Preceptor and given the posthumous title Zhongding, "Loyal and Settled."

sentences.zh: 初，伯彥既去相州，金人執其子軍器監丞似，使割地以至相州，守臣趙不試固守不下，遂拘而北，久之乃還。

translations.literal: Earlier, after Boyan had left Xiangzhou, the Jurchens seized his son Si, Supervisor of the Directorate of Armaments, and used him to demand ceded territory up to Xiangzhou. The defending official Zhao Bushi held firm and would not yield, so Si was taken north and only returned after a long time.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, after Boyan had left Xiangzhou, the Jurchens seized his son Si, Supervisor of the Directorate of Armaments, and used him to demand territory up to Xiangzhou; the defending official Zhao Bushi held firm and refused to yield, so Si was taken north and only returned after a long captivity.

sentences.zh: 或云似之得歸，伯彥實使人贖之。

translations.literal: Some said that when Si was able to return, Boyan had in fact sent men to ransom him.
translations.idiomatic: Some said that when Si finally came home, Boyan had in fact sent men to ransom him.

sentences.zh: 似後更名召嗣。

translations.literal: Si later changed his name to Zhaosi.
translations.idiomatic: Si later changed his name to Zhaosi.

sentences.zh: 時議割三鎮以弭兵，命檜借禮部侍郎與程瑀為割地使，奉肅王以往。

translations.literal: At the time there was discussion of ceding the Three Prefectures to stop the war. Hui was ordered to serve temporarily as Vice Minister of Rites and, with Cheng Yu, go as cession envoy, escorting Prince Su.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the court debated ceding the Three Prefectures to halt the war; Hui was temporarily appointed Vice Minister of Rites and, together with Cheng Yu, sent as cession envoy escorting Prince Su.

sentences.zh: 金師退，檜、瑀至燕而還。

translations.literal: When the Jurchen army withdrew, Hui and Yu reached Yan and returned.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jurchen army withdrew, Hui and Yu reached Yan and returned.

sentences.zh: 御史中丞李回、翰林承旨吳幵共薦檜，拜殿中侍御史，遷左司諫。

translations.literal: Censor-in-Chief Li Hui and Hanlin Academician-in-Attendance Wu Qian jointly recommended Hui. He was appointed Palace Censor and then promoted to Left Remonstrator.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-Chief Li Hui and Hanlin Academician-in-Attendance Wu Qian jointly recommended Hui; he was appointed Palace Censor and then promoted to Left Remonstrator.

sentences.zh: 王雲、李若水見金二酋歸，言金堅欲得地，不然，進兵取汴京。

translations.literal: Wang Yun and Li Ruoshui, returning after meeting the two Jurchen chiefs, said the Jurchens firmly wanted territory; otherwise they would advance and take Bianjing.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yun and Li Ruoshui, returning from meeting the two Jurchen chiefs, reported that the Jurchens were determined to have the territory—or else they would advance and take Bianjing.

sentences.zh: 十一月，集百官議於延和殿，范宗尹等七十人請與之，檜等三十六人持不可。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month the officials were assembled to deliberate in the Yanshe Hall. Fan Zongyin and seventy others asked to grant it; Hui and thirty-six others held that it could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month the officials were assembled to deliberate in the Yanshe Hall; Fan Zongyin and seventy others favored cession, while Hui and thirty-six others opposed it.

sentences.zh: 未幾，除御史中丞。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was appointed Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 閏十一月，汴京失守，二帝幸金營。

translations.literal: In the intercalary eleventh month Bianjing fell. The two emperors went to the Jurchen camp.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary eleventh month Bianjing fell, and the two emperors were taken to the Jurchen camp.

sentences.zh: 二年二月，莫儔、吳幵自金營來，傳金帥命推立異姓。

translations.literal: In the second year, second month, Mo Chou and Wu Qian came from the Jurchen camp bearing the Jurchen commander's order to establish a ruler of another surname.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, second month, Mo Chou and Wu Qian came from the Jurchen camp with the Jurchen commander's order to install a ruler of another surname.

sentences.zh: 留守王時雍等召百官軍民共議立張邦昌，皆失色不敢答，監察御史馬伸言於眾曰：「吾曹職為爭臣，豈容坐視不吐一辭？

translations.literal: Left-behind official Wang Shiyong and others summoned officials, soldiers, and people to discuss jointly installing Zhang Bangchang. All turned pale and dared not answer. Supervising Censor Ma Shen said to the assembly: "Our office is to remonstrate. How can we sit by and not speak a word?
translations.idiomatic: Left-behind official Wang Shiyong and others summoned officials, soldiers, and civilians to discuss installing Zhang Bangchang; all turned pale and dared not speak. Supervising Censor Ma Shen addressed the assembly: "Our duty is to remonstrate—how can we sit by in silence?

sentences.zh: 當共入議狀，乞存趙氏。」

translations.literal: We should jointly enter a deliberation petition asking to preserve the Zhao house."
translations.idiomatic: We should jointly submit a deliberation petition asking that the Zhao house be preserved."

sentences.zh: 時檜為台長，聞伸言以為然，即進狀曰：

translations.literal: At the time Hui was chief of the censorate. Hearing Shen's words he agreed, and at once submitted a petition saying:
translations.idiomatic: Hui was then chief of the censorate; hearing Shen's words he agreed, and at once submitted a petition stating:

sentences.zh: 檜荷國厚恩，甚愧無報。

translations.literal: Hui has received the state's deep grace and is greatly ashamed at having no repayment.
translations.idiomatic: Hui has received the state's deep favor and is deeply ashamed to have repaid so little.

sentences.zh: 今金人擁重兵，臨已拔之城，操生殺之柄，必欲易姓，檜盡死以辨，非特忠於主也，且明兩國之利害爾。

translations.literal: Now the Jurchens hold a great army, stand before a city already taken, and wield the power of life and death. They insist on changing the dynasty. Hui would exhaust death in argument—not only out of loyalty to his ruler, but also to clarify the interests of both states.
translations.idiomatic: Now the Jurchens hold a great army before a city already taken and wield the power of life and death; insisting on changing the dynasty, they would have us submit. Hui would die arguing the point—not only from loyalty to his sovereign, but to make clear the interests of both states.

sentences.zh: 趙氏自祖宗以至嗣君，百七十餘載。

translations.literal: The Zhao house from the ancestors down to the reigning lord has endured more than one hundred and seventy years.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhao house has ruled from the founding ancestors down to the present sovereign for more than one hundred and seventy years.

sentences.zh: 頃緣奸臣敗盟，結怨鄰國，謀臣失計，誤主喪師，遂致生靈被禍，京都失守，主上出郊，求和軍前。

translations.literal: Recently, because treacherous ministers broke the alliance and incurred the enmity of a neighboring state, and strategists lost their plans and misled the ruler into losing armies, the people suffered calamity, the capital fell, the sovereign went out beyond the city to seek peace before the enemy army.
translations.idiomatic: Recently treacherous ministers broke the alliance and earned the enmity of a neighboring state; strategists blundered and led the sovereign to lose his armies—so the people suffered, the capital fell, and the emperor went out beyond the walls to sue for peace before the enemy host.

sentences.zh: 兩元帥既允其議，布聞中外矣，且空竭帑藏，追取服禦所用，割兩河地，恭為臣子，今乃變易前議，人臣安忍畏死不論哉？

translations.literal: The two commanders already agreed to the terms and announced them inside and outside the court. The treasury was emptied, imperial robes and accoutrements were seized, the lands of the two He regions were ceded, and we submitted as subjects. Now to change the prior agreement—how can a minister bear to keep silent for fear of death?
translations.idiomatic: The two Jurchen commanders had already agreed to terms and proclaimed them throughout the realm; the treasury was emptied, imperial robes and accoutrements seized, the lands of the two He regions ceded, and we submitted as vassals—yet now they would change what was agreed. What minister could keep silent for fear of death?

sentences.zh: 宋於中國，號令一統，綿地萬里，德澤加于百姓，前古未有。

translations.literal: Song within the Central Realm unified command, extended over ten thousand li, and bestowed virtue and grace upon the common people as no earlier age had.
translations.idiomatic: Song ruled the Central Realm with unified authority, its domain stretching ten thousand li, bestowing virtue and grace upon the people as no earlier age had done.

sentences.zh: 雖興亡之命在天有數，焉可以一城決廢立哉？

translations.literal: Although the fate of rise and fall is in Heaven and has its number, how can one decide deposition and installation by a single city?
translations.idiomatic: Though the fate of rise and fall lies with Heaven and has its appointed course, how can the fate of a dynasty be decided by the fall of a single city?

sentences.zh: 昔西漢絕於新室，光武以興；

translations.literal: Formerly Western Han ended with the Xin dynasty, and Guangwu rose to restore it;
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Western Han ended with Wang Mang's Xin dynasty, and Guangwu rose to restore it;

sentences.zh: 東漢絕于曹氏，劉備帝蜀；

translations.literal: Eastern Han ended with the Cao house, and Liu Bei reigned in Shu;
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Han ended with the house of Cao, and Liu Bei reigned in Shu;

sentences.zh: 唐為朱溫篡奪，李克用猶推其世序而繼之。

translations.literal: Tang was usurped by Zhu Wen, yet Li Keyong still upheld its dynastic line and succeeded it.
translations.idiomatic: Tang was usurped by Zhu Wen, yet Li Keyong still upheld its dynastic succession.

sentences.zh: 蓋基廣則難傾，根深則難拔。

translations.literal: For when the foundation is broad it is hard to overturn, and when the roots are deep they are hard to uproot.
translations.idiomatic: For when the foundation is broad it is hard to overturn, and when the roots run deep they are hard to uproot.

sentences.zh: 張邦昌在上皇時，附會權幸，共為蠹國之政。

translations.literal: Zhang Bangchang, in the time of the Retired Emperor, attached himself to the powerful and together they enacted policies that harmed the state.
translations.idiomatic: In the time of the Retired Emperor, Zhang Bangchang attached himself to the powerful and together they enacted policies that ruined the state.

sentences.zh: 社稷傾危，生民塗炭，固非一人所致，亦邦昌為之也。

translations.literal: The altars of state were endangered and the people were plunged into suffering. It was not caused by one man alone, yet Bangchang was among those who did it.
translations.idiomatic: The altars of state were endangered and the people plunged into suffering—not the work of one man alone, yet Bangchang was among those responsible.

sentences.zh: 天下方疾之如仇讎，若付以土地，使主人民，四方豪傑必共起而誅之，終不足為大金屏翰。

translations.literal: The realm now hates him as an enemy. If land were entrusted to him to rule the people, heroes throughout the four directions would surely rise together to punish him. In the end he would not suffice as a bulwark for Great Jin.
translations.idiomatic: The realm now hates him as a mortal enemy; if territory were entrusted to him to rule the people, heroes throughout the land would surely rise to destroy him—and in the end he would never serve Great Jin as a reliable bulwark.

sentences.zh: 必立邦昌，則京師之民可服，天下之民不可服；

translations.literal: If Bangchang must be installed, the people of the capital may be made to submit, but the people of the realm cannot be made to submit;
translations.idiomatic: If Bangchang must be installed, the people of the capital may be compelled to submit, but the people of the realm cannot;

sentences.zh: 京師之宗子可滅，天下之宗子不可滅。

translations.literal: The imperial clansmen of the capital may be destroyed, but the imperial clansmen of the realm cannot be destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial clansmen of the capital may be wiped out, but the imperial clansmen throughout the realm cannot be.

sentences.zh: 檜不顧斧鉞之誅，言兩朝之利害，願復嗣君位以安四方，非特大宋蒙福，亦大金萬世利也。

translations.literal: Hui, heedless of execution by axe and halberd, spoke of the interests of both dynasties and wished to restore the heir to the throne to settle the four directions—not only would Great Song receive blessing, but Great Jin would also gain benefit for ten thousand generations.
translations.idiomatic: Hui, heedless of death by axe and halberd, argued the interests of both dynasties and urged restoring the heir to the throne to pacify the realm—not only would Great Song be blessed, but Great Jin would gain lasting benefit as well.

sentences.zh: 檜之歸也，自言殺金人監己者奔舟而來。

translations.literal: When Hui returned, he himself said he had killed the Jurchen who guarded him and fled by boat.
translations.idiomatic: On his return, Hui claimed that he had killed his Jurchen guard and fled south by boat.

sentences.zh: 朝士多謂檜與㮚傅、樸同拘，而檜獨歸；

translations.literal: Many court officials said that Hui had been detained together with Li Fu and Pu, yet Hui alone returned;
translations.idiomatic: Many at court noted that Hui had been detained together with Li Fu and Pu, yet Hui alone had returned;

sentences.zh: 又自燕至楚二千八百里，逾河越海，豈無譏訶之者，安得殺監而南？

translations.literal: Moreover, from Yan to Chu was twenty-eight hundred li, crossing rivers and seas—would there not have been those who mocked and reproached him? How could he have killed his guard and come south?
translations.idiomatic: moreover, the journey from Yan to Chu was twenty-eight hundred li, crossing rivers and seas—would no one have challenged him? How could he have killed his guard and made it south?

sentences.zh: 就令從軍撻懶，金人縱之，必質妻屬，安得與王氏偕？

translations.literal: Even if he had followed the army of Tatala, and the Jurchens released him, they would surely have held his wife and family as hostages—how could he have traveled together with Lady Wang?
translations.idiomatic: Even if he had followed Tatala's army and the Jurchens released him, they would surely have held his family as hostages—how could he have traveled with Lady Wang?

sentences.zh: 惟宰相范宗尹、同知樞密院李回與檜善，盡破群疑，力薦其忠。

translations.literal: Only Chief Minister Fan Zongyin and Vice Commissioner of Military Affairs Li Hui were friendly with Hui. They dispelled all the doubts of the crowd and strongly recommended his loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: Only Chief Minister Fan Zongyin and Vice Commissioner of Military Affairs Li Hui were on good terms with Hui; they dispelled the widespread doubts and strongly vouched for his loyalty.

sentences.zh: 未對前一日，帝命先見宰執。

translations.literal: The day before his audience, the emperor ordered him to see the chief ministers first.
translations.idiomatic: The day before his formal audience, the emperor ordered him to meet the chief ministers first.

sentences.zh: 檜首言「如欲天下無事，南自南，北自北」，及首奏所草與撻懶求和書。

translations.literal: Hui first spoke the words "If you wish the realm to be at peace, let the south be the south and the north be the north," and first memorialized the peace letter he had drafted for Tatala.
translations.idiomatic: Hui opened with the formula "If you wish the realm to be at peace, let the south be the south and the north be the north," and presented the peace letter he had drafted for Tatala.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「檜樸忠過人，朕得之喜而不寐。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Hui's plain loyalty surpasses others. Gaining him, I am so pleased I cannot sleep.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Hui's plain loyalty surpasses that of others—I am so delighted to have found him that I cannot sleep.

sentences.zh: 蓋聞二帝、母后消息，又得一佳士也。」

translations.literal: For I have heard news of the two emperors and the empress dowager, and have also gained an excellent man."
translations.idiomatic: I have heard news of the two emperors and the empress dowager, and have gained an excellent man as well."

sentences.zh: 宗尹欲處之經筵，帝曰：「且與一事簡尚書。」

translations.literal: Zongyin wished to place him in the imperial lecture hall. The emperor said: "For now give him charge of a ministry with lighter duties."
translations.idiomatic: Zongyin wished to place him in the imperial lecture hall, but the emperor said, "For now give him charge of a ministry with lighter duties."

sentences.zh: 故有禮部之命。

translations.literal: Therefore there was the appointment to the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Hence the appointment to the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 從行王安道、馮由義、水砦丁不異及參議官並改京秩，舟人孫靖亦補承信郎。

translations.literal: Wang Andao, Feng Youyi, Ding Buyi of the Water Fort, and the advisory officials who traveled with him were all transferred to capital ranks. The boatman Sun Jing was also granted the rank of Credentialed Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Andao, Feng Youyi, Ding Buyi of the Water Fort, and the advisory officials who had traveled with him were all promoted to capital ranks; the boatman Sun Jing was also granted the rank of Credentialed Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 始，朝廷雖數遣使，但且守且和，而專與金人解仇議和，實自檜始。

translations.literal: At the beginning, although the court had sent envoys several times, it had only held while negotiating peace. But to devote oneself exclusively to resolving enmity and negotiating peace with the Jurchens truly began with Hui.
translations.idiomatic: Although the court had sent envoys several times before, holding the line while negotiating peace, the policy of seeking reconciliation and peace exclusively with the Jurchens truly began with Hui.

sentences.zh: 蓋檜在金庭首唱和議，故撻懶縱之使歸也。

translations.literal: For Hui had been the first at the Jurchen court to advocate peace talks, and therefore Tatala released him to return.
translations.idiomatic: Hui had been the first at the Jurchen court to advocate peace talks, and that was why Tatala released him to return.

sentences.zh: 紹興元年二月，除參知政事。

translations.literal: In the second month of the first year of Shaoxing, he was appointed Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the first year of Shaoxing, he was appointed Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 七月，宗尹罷。

translations.literal: In the seventh month Zongyin was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Zongyin was dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 先是，范宗尹建議討論崇甯、大觀以來濫賞，檜力贊其議，見帝意堅，反以此擠之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Fan Zongyin had proposed reviewing excessive rewards since the Chongning and Daguan eras. Hui strongly endorsed the proposal, but seeing the emperor's resolve firm, he turned and used it to squeeze Zongyin out.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Fan Zongyin had proposed reviewing excessive rewards since the Chongning and Daguan eras; Hui strongly endorsed the idea, but when he saw the emperor's resolve, he turned and used it to drive Zongyin out.

sentences.zh: 宗尹既去，相位久虛。

translations.literal: After Zongyin departed, the chief ministership stood vacant for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: After Zongyin left office, the chief ministership remained vacant for a long time.

sentences.zh: 檜揚言曰：「我有二策，可聳動天下。」

translations.literal: Hui proclaimed publicly: "I have two strategies that can shake the whole realm."
translations.idiomatic: Hui proclaimed publicly, "I have two strategies that could shake the whole realm."

sentences.zh: 或問何以不言，檜曰：「今無相，不可行也。」

translations.literal: When someone asked why he did not speak of them, Hui said: "There is no chief minister now—it cannot be done."
translations.idiomatic: When someone asked why he would not reveal them, Hui said, "There is no chief minister now—it cannot be done."

sentences.zh: 八月，拜右僕射、同中書門下平章事兼知樞密院事。

translations.literal: In the eighth month he was appointed Right Vice Director, Co-Grand Councillor of the Secretariat-Chancellery, and concurrent Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month he was appointed Right Vice Director, Co-Grand Councillor of the Secretariat-Chancellery, and concurrent Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 九月，呂頤浩再相，檜同秉政，謀奪其柄，風其黨建言：「周宣王內修外攘，故能中興，今二相宜分任內外。」

translations.literal: In the ninth month Lü Yihao became chief minister again. Hui shared power and plotted to seize his authority. He prompted his faction to propose: "King Xuan of Zhou strengthened the interior and repelled external foes, and so was able to restore the dynasty. The two chief ministers today should divide duties between interior and exterior."
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Lü Yihao returned as chief minister; Hui shared power and plotted to seize his authority, prompting his faction to propose, "King Xuan of Zhou strengthened the interior and repelled external foes and so restored the dynasty—the two chief ministers today should divide duties between civil and military affairs."

sentences.zh: 頤浩遂建都督府于鎮江。

translations.literal: Yihao then established a supreme command headquarters at Zhenjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Yihao then established a supreme command headquarters at Zhenjiang.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「頤浩專治軍旅，檜專理庶務，如種、蠡之分職可也。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Let Yihao specialize in military affairs and Hui in civil administration—like the division of labor between Wen Zhong and Fan Li."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Let Yihao handle military affairs and Hui civil administration—like the division of labor between Wen Zhong and Fan Li."

sentences.zh: 二年，檜奏置修政局，自為提舉，參知政事翟汝文同領之。

translations.literal: In the second year Hui memorialized to establish a Bureau for Political Reform, making himself its supervisor, with Vice Director Zhai Ruwen as co-director.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year Hui memorialized to establish a Bureau for Political Reform, appointing himself supervisor with Vice Director Zhai Ruwen as co-director.

sentences.zh: 未幾，檜面劾汝文擅治堂吏，汝文求去；

translations.literal: Before long Hui impeached Ruwen to his face for overstepping authority in managing chancery clerks, and Ruwen requested to leave;
translations.idiomatic: Before long Hui openly impeached Ruwen for overstepping authority in managing chancery clerks, and Ruwen requested to resign;

sentences.zh: 諫官方孟卿一再論之，汝文竟罷。

translations.literal: Remonstrator Fang Mengqing argued the matter repeatedly, and Ruwen was finally dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrator Fang Mengqing argued the case repeatedly, and Ruwen was finally removed from office.

sentences.zh: 監察御史劉一止，檜黨也，言：「宣王內修，修其所謂外攘之政而已。

translations.literal: Supervising Censor Liu Yizhi, a member of Hui's faction, said: "When King Xuan strengthened the interior, he reformed what was called the policy of repelling external foes—that is all.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Censor Liu Yizhi, a member of Hui's faction, said, "When King Xuan strengthened the interior, he reformed what was called the policy of repelling external foes—that is all.

sentences.zh: 今簿書獄訟、官吏差除、土木營繕俱非所當急者。」

translations.literal: Now documents and lawsuits, appointments and dismissals of officials, and construction and repairs are none of what should be urgent."
translations.idiomatic: Documents and lawsuits, appointments and dismissals, construction and repairs—none of these should be urgent priorities now."

sentences.zh: 屯田郎曾統亦謂檜曰：「宰相事無不統，何以局為？」

translations.literal: Gentleman of the Bureau of Agriculture Zeng Tong also said to Hui: "A chief minister's affairs are all-encompassing—why need a bureau?"
translations.idiomatic: Gentleman of the Bureau of Agriculture Zeng Tong also said to Hui, "A chief minister's affairs are all-encompassing—why need a separate bureau?"

sentences.zh: 檜皆不聽。

translations.literal: Hui would not listen to any of them.
translations.idiomatic: Hui would not listen to any of them.

sentences.zh: 既而有議廢局以搖檜者，一止及檢討官林待聘皆上疏言不可廢。

translations.literal: Then, when there was talk of abolishing the bureau to undermine Hui, Yizhi and Compiler Lin Daipin both submitted memorials saying it must not be abolished.
translations.idiomatic: When talk arose of abolishing the bureau to undermine Hui, Yizhi and Compiler Lin Daipin both submitted memorials arguing it must not be abolished.

sentences.zh: 七月，一止出臺，除起居郎，蓋自叛其說，識者笑之。

translations.literal: In the seventh month Yizhi left the censorate and was appointed Diarist—a betrayal of his own words, and the knowing laughed at him.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Yizhi left the censorate and was appointed Diarist—a reversal of his own position that made the knowing laugh.

sentences.zh: 頤浩自江上還，謀逐檜，有教以引朱勝非為助者。

translations.literal: When Yihao returned from the river region, he plotted to drive out Hui. Someone advised him to bring in Zhu Shengfei as an ally.
translations.idiomatic: When Yihao returned from the river region, he plotted to drive out Hui; someone advised him to bring in Zhu Shengfei as an ally.

sentences.zh: 詔以勝非同都督。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Shengfei co-supreme commander.
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed Shengfei co-supreme commander.

sentences.zh: 給事中胡安國言勝非不可用，勝非遂以醴泉觀使兼侍讀。

translations.literal: Drafting Reviewer Hu Anguo said Shengfei was unfit for use. Shengfei was then made Director of the Liquan Temple and concurrent Lecturer.
translations.idiomatic: Drafting Reviewer Hu Anguo argued that Shengfei was unfit for the post; Shengfei was then made Director of the Liquan Temple and concurrent Lecturer.

sentences.zh: 安國求去，檜三上章留之，不報。

translations.literal: Anguo requested to leave. Hui submitted three memorials asking to keep him, but received no reply.
translations.idiomatic: Anguo requested to resign; Hui submitted three memorials asking to keep him, but received no reply.

sentences.zh: 頤浩尋以黃龜年為殿中侍御史，劉棐為右司諫，蓋將逐檜。

translations.literal: Yihao soon appointed Huang Guinian as Palace Censor and Liu Fei as Right Remonstrator—clearly intending to drive out Hui.
translations.idiomatic: Yihao soon appointed Huang Guinian as Palace Censor and Liu Fei as Right Remonstrator—clearly preparing to drive out Hui.

sentences.zh: 於是江躋、吳表臣、程瑀、張燾、胡世將、劉一止、林待聘、樓炤並落職予祠，台省一空，皆檜黨也。

translations.literal: Thereupon Jiang Ji, Wu Biaochen, Cheng Yu, Zhang Tao, Hu Shijiang, Liu Yizhi, Lin Daipin, and Lou Zhao were all stripped of office and given temple commissions. The censorate and remonstrance offices were emptied—all were Hui's faction.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Jiang Ji, Wu Biaochen, Cheng Yu, Zhang Tao, Hu Shijiang, Liu Yizhi, Lin Daipin, and Lou Zhao were all stripped of office and given temple commissions; the censorate and remonstrance offices were emptied—all were members of Hui's faction.

sentences.zh: 檜初欲傾頤浩，引一時名賢如安國、燾、瑀輩布列清要。

translations.literal: At first, when Hui wished to overthrow Yihao, he brought in celebrated men of the time such as Anguo, Tao, and Yu and placed them in prestigious posts.
translations.idiomatic: At first, when Hui sought to overthrow Yihao, he brought in celebrated men of the time such as Anguo, Tao, and Yu and placed them in prestigious posts.

sentences.zh: 頤浩問去檜之術于席益，益曰：「目為黨可也。

translations.literal: Yihao asked Xi Yi the method for removing Hui. Yi said: "Label him a faction—that will do.
translations.idiomatic: Yihao asked Xi Yi how to remove Hui; Yi said, "Label him a faction—that will do.

sentences.zh: 今黨魁胡安國在瑣闥，宜先去之。」

translations.literal: Now the faction leader Hu Anguo is in the drafting office—you should remove him first."
translations.idiomatic: The faction leader Hu Anguo is now in the drafting office—you should remove him first."

sentences.zh: 蓋安國嘗問人材于遊酢，酢以檜為言，且比之荀文若。

translations.literal: For Anguo had once asked You Zuo about men of talent. Zuo spoke of Hui and compared him to Xun Wenruo.
translations.idiomatic: Anguo had once asked You Zuo about men of talent; Zuo spoke of Hui and compared him to Xun Wenruo.

sentences.zh: 故安國力言檜賢于張浚諸人，檜亦力引安國。

translations.literal: Therefore Anguo strongly declared Hui more worthy than Zhang Jun and the others, and Hui also strongly recommended Anguo.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore Anguo strongly declared Hui more worthy than Zhang Jun and the others, and Hui strongly recommended Anguo in return.

sentences.zh: 至是，安國等去，檜亦尋去。

translations.literal: By this time Anguo and the others had gone, and Hui soon followed.
translations.idiomatic: By then Anguo and the others were gone, and Hui soon followed.

sentences.zh: 檜再相誤國，安國已死矣。

translations.literal: When Hui became chief minister again and harmed the state, Anguo was already dead.
translations.idiomatic: By the time Hui became chief minister again and harmed the state, Anguo was already dead.

sentences.zh: 黃龜年始劾檜專主和議，沮止恢復，植黨專權，漸不可長，至比檜為莽、卓。

translations.literal: Huang Guinian first impeached Hui for monopolizing peace talks, obstructing recovery, planting a faction and monopolizing power—an evil that could not be allowed to grow—and even compared Hui to Wang Mang and Dong Zhuo.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Guinian first impeached Hui for monopolizing peace talks, obstructing recovery, building a faction and hoarding power—an evil that could not be allowed to grow—and even compared him to Wang Mang and Dong Zhuo.

sentences.zh: 八月，檜罷，乃為觀文殿學士、提舉江州太平觀。

translations.literal: In the eighth month Hui was dismissed and made Academician of the Hall for Viewing Literature and Director of the Taiping Temple in Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Hui was dismissed and made Academician of the Hall for Viewing Literature and Director of the Taiping Temple in Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 前一日，上召直學士院綦崈禮入對，示以檜所陳二策，欲以河北人還金國，中原人還劉豫。

translations.literal: The day before, the emperor summoned Academician Qi Chongli for an audience and showed him the two strategies Hui had proposed: to return people of Hebei to the Jin state and people of the Central Plain to Liu Yu.
translations.idiomatic: The day before, the emperor summoned Academician Qi Chongli and showed him the two strategies Hui had proposed: returning people of Hebei to the Jin state and people of the Central Plain to Liu Yu.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「檜言『南人歸南，北人歸北』。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Hui said 'Southerners return to the south, northerners return to the north.'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Hui said, 'Southerners return to the south, northerners return to the north.'

sentences.zh: 朕北人，將安歸？

translations.literal: I am a northerner—where am I to return?
translations.idiomatic: I am a northerner—where am I to return?

sentences.zh: 檜又言『為相數月，可聳動天下』，今無聞。」

translations.literal: Hui also said 'As chief minister for several months, I can shake the whole realm'—yet now nothing is heard of it."
translations.idiomatic: Hui also said, 'As chief minister for several months, I can shake the whole realm'—yet now nothing has come of it."

sentences.zh: 崈禮即以上意載訓辭，播告中外，人始知檜之奸。

translations.literal: Chongli at once recorded the emperor's intent in the dismissal edict and proclaimed it inside and outside the court. People then first learned of Hui's treachery.
translations.idiomatic: Chongli at once recorded the emperor's intent in the dismissal edict and proclaimed it throughout the realm; only then did people learn of Hui's treachery.

sentences.zh: 龜年等論檜不已，詔落職，榜朝堂，示不復用。

translations.literal: Guinian and others continued to denounce Hui without cease. An edict stripped his office, posted the notice in the court hall, and showed he would not be used again.
translations.idiomatic: Guinian and others kept denouncing Hui without cease; an edict stripped his rank, posted the notice in the court hall, and declared he would not be used again.

sentences.zh: 三年，韓肖胄等使還，洎金使李永壽、王翊偕來，求盡還北俘，與檜前議吻合。

translations.literal: In the third year Han Xiaozhou and others returned as envoys. When Jin envoys Li Yongshou and Wang Yi came together, they asked that all northern captives be returned—a request matching Hui's earlier proposal.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year Han Xiaozhou and others returned as envoys; when Jin envoys Li Yongshou and Wang Yi arrived together, they demanded the return of all northern captives—a request that matched Hui's earlier proposal.

sentences.zh: 識者益知檜與金人共謀，國家之辱未已也。

translations.literal: The knowing increasingly understood that Hui had conspired with the Jurchens, and the nation's humiliation was not yet ended.
translations.idiomatic: The knowing increasingly understood that Hui had conspired with the Jurchens, and the nation's humiliation was far from over.

sentences.zh: 五年，金主既死，撻懶主議，卒成其和。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, after the Jin ruler died, Tatala led the deliberations and finally brought the peace to completion.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, after the Jin ruler died, Tatala led the peace negotiations and finally brought the treaty to completion.

sentences.zh: 二月，復資政殿學士，仍舊宮祠。

translations.literal: In the second month his rank as Academician of the Hall for Assisting Governance was restored, and he retained his old temple commission.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month his rank as Academician of the Hall for Assisting Governance was restored, and he retained his old temple commission.

sentences.zh: 六月，除觀文殿學士、知溫州。

translations.literal: In the sixth month he was appointed Academician of the Hall for Viewing Literature and Prefect of Wenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month he was appointed Academician of the Hall for Viewing Literature and Prefect of Wenzhou.

sentences.zh: 六年七月，改知紹興府。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the sixth year he was transferred to Prefect of Shaoxing.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the sixth year he was transferred to Prefect of Shaoxing.

sentences.zh: 尋除醴泉觀使兼侍讀，充行宮留守；

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Director of the Liquan Temple and concurrent Lecturer, serving as left-behind official of the traveling palace;
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was appointed Director of the Liquan Temple and concurrent Lecturer, serving as left-behind official of the traveling palace;

sentences.zh: 孟庾同留守，並權赴尚書、樞密院參決庶事。

translations.literal: Meng Yu served as co-left-behind official, and both were authorized to attend the Department of State Affairs and Bureau of Military Affairs to decide civil affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Yu served as co-left-behind official, and both were authorized to attend the Department of State Affairs and Bureau of Military Affairs to decide civil affairs.

sentences.zh: 時已降詔將行幸，檜乞扈從，不許。

translations.literal: An edict had already been issued for the imperial progress. Hui asked to accompany the emperor and was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: An edict had already been issued for the imperial progress; Hui asked to accompany the emperor and was refused.

sentences.zh: 帝駐蹕平江，召檜赴行在，用右相張浚薦也。

translations.literal: When the emperor halted at Pingjiang, he summoned Hui to the traveling court on the recommendation of Right Chief Minister Zhang Jun.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor halted at Pingjiang, he summoned Hui to the traveling court on the recommendation of Right Chief Minister Zhang Jun.

sentences.zh: 十二月，檜以醴泉觀兼侍讀赴講筵。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month Hui attended the lecture hall as Director of the Liquan Temple and concurrent Lecturer.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Hui attended the lecture hall as Director of the Liquan Temple and concurrent Lecturer.

sentences.zh: 七年正月，何蘚使金還，得徽宗及寧德后訃，帝號慟發喪，即日授檜樞密使，恩數視宰臣。

translations.literal: In the first month of the seventh year He Xian returned from an embassy to Jin with news of the deaths of Emperor Huizong and Empress Ningde. The emperor wailed and began mourning. That same day Hui was appointed Commissioner of Military Affairs with honors equal to a chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the seventh year He Xian returned from an embassy to Jin with news of the deaths of Emperor Huizong and Empress Ningde; the emperor wailed and began mourning, and that same day appointed Hui Commissioner of Military Affairs with honors equal to a chief minister.

sentences.zh: 四月，命王倫使金國迎奉梓宮。

translations.literal: In the fourth month Wang Lun was ordered to go as envoy to the Jin state to receive the imperial coffin.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month Wang Lun was ordered to go as envoy to the Jin state to receive the imperial coffin.

sentences.zh: 九月，浚求去，帝問：「誰可代卿？」

translations.literal: In the ninth month Jun requested to leave. The emperor asked: "Who can replace you?"
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Jun requested to resign; the emperor asked, "Who can replace you?"

sentences.zh: 浚不對。

translations.literal: Jun did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: Jun did not answer.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「秦檜何如？」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "What of Qin Hui?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "What of Qin Hui?"

sentences.zh: 浚曰：「與之共事，始知其暗。」

translations.literal: Jun said: "Working with him, I have only now learned how treacherous he is."
translations.idiomatic: Jun said, "Working with him, I have only now learned how treacherous he is."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「然則用趙鼎。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Then use Zhao Ding."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Then use Zhao Ding."

sentences.zh: 鼎於是復相。

translations.literal: Ding then became chief minister again.
translations.idiomatic: Ding then returned as chief minister.

sentences.zh: 台諫交章論浚，安置嶺表。

translations.literal: Censors and remonstrators submitted successive memorials against Jun, and he was assigned to the Lingnan region.
translations.idiomatic: Censors and remonstrators submitted successive memorials against Jun, and he was exiled to the Lingnan region.

sentences.zh: 鼎約同列救解。

translations.literal: Ding agreed with his colleagues to plead for Jun's release.
translations.idiomatic: Ding agreed with his colleagues to plead for Jun's release.

sentences.zh: 與張守面奏，各數千百言，檜獨無一語。

translations.literal: Together with Zhang Shou he memorialized in person, each speaking thousands of words, but Hui alone said not a word.
translations.idiomatic: Together with Zhang Shou he memorialized in person, each speaking at length, but Hui alone said not a word.

sentences.zh: 浚遂謫永州。

translations.literal: Jun was then demoted to Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Jun was then demoted to Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 始，浚、鼎相得甚，浚先達，力引鼎。

translations.literal: At the beginning Jun and Ding got on very well. Jun rose first and strongly recommended Ding.
translations.idiomatic: At first Jun and Ding were on excellent terms; Jun rose first and strongly recommended Ding.

sentences.zh: 嘗共論人才，浚劇談檜善，鼎曰：「此人得志，吾人無所措足矣！」

translations.literal: They once discussed men of talent together. Jun spoke at length of Hui's virtues. Ding said: "If this man gets his way, we will have nowhere to stand!"
translations.idiomatic: They once discussed men of talent together; Jun spoke at length of Hui's virtues, and Ding said, "If this man gets his way, we will have nowhere to stand!"

sentences.zh: 浚不以為然，故引檜，共政方知其暗，不復再薦也。

translations.literal: Jun did not agree, and therefore recommended Hui. Only after sharing power did he learn how treacherous Hui was, and he never recommended him again.
translations.idiomatic: Jun disagreed and therefore recommended Hui; only after sharing power did he learn how treacherous Hui was, and he never recommended him again.

sentences.zh: 檜因此憾浚，反謂鼎曰：「上欲召公，而張相遲留。」

translations.literal: Hui therefore resented Jun and in turn told Ding: "The emperor wishes to summon you, but Chief Minister Zhang is delaying."
translations.idiomatic: Hui therefore resented Jun and told Ding in turn, "The emperor wishes to summon you, but Chief Minister Zhang is delaying."

sentences.zh: 蓋怒鼎使擠浚也。

translations.literal: This was because he was angry at Ding and wanted to use him to squeeze out Jun.
translations.idiomatic: This was because he was angry at Ding and wanted to use him to drive out Jun.

sentences.zh: 檜在樞府惟聽鼎，鼎素惡檜，由是反深信之，卒為所傾。

translations.literal: In the Bureau of Military Affairs Hui deferred entirely to Ding. Ding had always disliked Hui, but for this reason came instead to trust him deeply and was ultimately overthrown by him.
translations.idiomatic: In the Bureau of Military Affairs Hui deferred entirely to Ding; Ding had always disliked Hui, but for this reason came instead to trust him deeply and was ultimately overthrown by him.

sentences.zh: 鼎與浚晚遇於閩，言及此，始知皆為檜所賣。

translations.literal: Ding and Jun met late in Min and spoke of this, and only then learned they had both been betrayed by Hui.
translations.idiomatic: Ding and Jun met late in life in Min and spoke of this; only then did they learn they had both been betrayed by Hui.

sentences.zh: 十一月，奉使朱弁以書報粘罕死，帝曰：「金人暴虐，不亡何待？」

translations.literal: In the eleventh month the envoy Zhu Bian reported by letter that Nianhan had died. The emperor said: "The Jurchens are brutal and cruel—how can they not perish?"
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month envoy Zhu Bian reported by letter that Nianhan had died; the emperor said, "The Jurchens are brutal and cruel—how can they not perish?"

sentences.zh: 檜曰：「陛下但積德，中興固有時。」

translations.literal: Hui said: "Your Majesty need only accumulate virtue—the restoration will surely come in its time."
translations.idiomatic: Hui said, "Your Majesty need only accumulate virtue—the restoration will surely come in its time."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「此固有時，然亦須有所施為，然後可以得志。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "That time will surely come, but one must also take action before one can achieve one's aim."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "That time will surely come, but one must also take action before one can achieve one's aim."

sentences.zh: 八年三月，拜右僕射、同中書門下平章事兼樞密使。

translations.literal: In the third month of the eighth year he was appointed Right Vice Director, Co-Grand Councillor of the Secretariat-Chancellery, and concurrent Commissioner of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the eighth year he was appointed Right Vice Director, Co-Grand Councillor of the Secretariat-Chancellery, and concurrent Commissioner of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 吏部侍郎晏敦復有憂色，曰：「奸人相矣。」

translations.literal: Vice Minister of Personnel Yan Dunfu wore a troubled expression and said: "A villain is chief minister now."
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister of Personnel Yan Dunfu wore a troubled expression and said, "A villain is chief minister now."

sentences.zh: 五月，金遣烏陵思謀等來議和，與王倫偕至。

translations.literal: In the fifth month Jin sent Wulinsi Mou and others to negotiate peace, arriving together with Wang Lun.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Jin sent Wulinsi Mou and others to negotiate peace, arriving together with Wang Lun.

sentences.zh: 思謀即宣和始通好海上者。

translations.literal: Simou was the one who had first opened friendly relations at sea in the Xuanhe era.
translations.idiomatic: Simou was the man who had first opened friendly relations at sea in the Xuanhe era.

sentences.zh: 議以吏部侍郎魏矼館伴，矼辭曰：「頃任御史，嘗言和議之非，今不可專對。」

translations.literal: It was proposed that Vice Minister of Personnel Wei Kang serve as host. Kang declined, saying: "When I recently served as censor, I spoke against peace talks. I cannot now serve as sole negotiator."
translations.idiomatic: It was proposed that Vice Minister of Personnel Wei Kang serve as host; Kang declined, saying, "When I recently served as censor, I spoke against peace talks—I cannot now serve as sole negotiator."

sentences.zh: 檜問矼所以不主和，矼備言敵情。

translations.literal: Hui asked Kang why he did not favor peace. Kang fully explained the enemy's situation.
translations.idiomatic: Hui asked Kang why he opposed peace; Kang fully explained the enemy's situation.

sentences.zh: 檜曰：「公以智料敵，檜以誠待敵。」

translations.literal: Hui said: "You use wisdom to assess the enemy; I use sincerity to treat the enemy."
translations.idiomatic: Hui said, "You use wisdom to assess the enemy; I use sincerity to treat the enemy."

sentences.zh: 矼曰：「第恐敵不以誠待相公爾。」

translations.literal: Kang said: "I only fear the enemy will not treat the chief minister with sincerity."
translations.idiomatic: Kang said, "I only fear the enemy will not treat you with sincerity."

sentences.zh: 檜乃改命。

translations.literal: Hui then changed the appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Hui then changed the appointment.

sentences.zh: 六月，思謀等入見。

translations.literal: In the sixth month Simou and the others had an audience.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Simou and the others had an audience.

sentences.zh: 帝愀然謂宰相曰：「先帝梓宮，果有還期，雖待二三年尚庶幾。

translations.literal: The emperor said sorrowfully to the chief ministers: "If the late emperor's coffin truly has a date of return, even waiting two or three years would still be acceptable.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said sorrowfully to the chief ministers, "If the late emperor's coffin truly has a date of return, even waiting two or three years would still be acceptable.

sentences.zh: 惟是太后春秋高，朕旦夕思念，欲早相見，此所以不憚屈己，冀和議之速成也。」

translations.literal: Only the empress dowager is advanced in years, and I think of her morning and evening, wishing to see her soon. This is why I do not shrink from humbling myself, hoping the peace talks will be quickly concluded."
translations.idiomatic: Only the empress dowager is advanced in years, and I think of her constantly, longing to see her soon—that is why I do not shrink from humbling myself, hoping the peace talks will be quickly concluded."

sentences.zh: 檜曰：「屈己議和，此人主之孝也。

translations.literal: Hui said: "To humble oneself and negotiate peace—this is the sovereign's filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: Hui said, "To humble oneself and negotiate peace—this is the sovereign's filial piety.

sentences.zh: 見主卑屈，懷憤不平，此人臣之忠也。」

translations.literal: To see one's lord humbled and feel indignant and aggrieved—this is the minister's loyalty."
translations.idiomatic: To see one's lord humbled and feel indignant and aggrieved—this is a minister's loyalty."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「雖然，有備無患，使和議可成，邊備亦不可弛。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Even so, preparedness prevents disaster. Even if peace talks succeed, frontier defenses must not be relaxed."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Even so, preparedness prevents disaster—even if peace talks succeed, frontier defenses must not be relaxed."

sentences.zh: 十月，宰執入見，檜獨留身，言：「臣僚畏首尾，多持兩端，此不足與斷大事。

translations.literal: In the tenth month the chief ministers entered for an audience. Hui alone remained and said: "Officials fear consequences at both ends and mostly hold to both sides. They are not fit to decide great affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month the chief ministers entered for an audience; Hui alone remained and said, "Officials fear consequences at both ends and mostly hedge their bets—they are not fit to decide great affairs.

sentences.zh: 若陛下決欲講和，乞顓與臣議，勿許群臣預。」

translations.literal: If Your Majesty is resolved to negotiate peace, I beg that deliberation be entrusted to me alone and that the multitude of officials not be permitted to participate."
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty is resolved to negotiate peace, I beg that deliberation be entrusted to me alone and that other officials not be permitted to participate."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「朕獨委卿。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "I entrust this to you alone."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "I entrust this to you alone."

sentences.zh: 檜曰：「臣亦恐未便，望陛下更思三日，容臣別奏。」

translations.literal: Hui said: "I too fear it may not yet be expedient. I hope Your Majesty will consider further for three days and allow me to memorialize separately."
translations.idiomatic: Hui said, "I too fear it may not yet be expedient—I hope Your Majesty will consider further for three days and allow me to memorialize separately."

sentences.zh: 又三日，檜復留身奏事，帝意欲和甚堅，檜猶以為未也，曰：「臣恐別有未便，欲望陛下更思三日，容臣別奏。」

translations.literal: Three days later Hui again remained to memorialize. The emperor's intent for peace was very firm, yet Hui still thought it not yet settled and said: "I fear there may still be inexpediency. I hope Your Majesty will consider further for three days and allow me to memorialize separately."
translations.idiomatic: Three days later Hui again remained to memorialize; the emperor's intent for peace was very firm, yet Hui still held back and said, "I fear there may still be inexpediency—I hope Your Majesty will consider further for three days and allow me to memorialize separately."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「然。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "So be it."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "So be it."

sentences.zh: 又三日。

translations.literal: Three days passed again.
translations.idiomatic: Three more days passed.

sentences.zh: 檜復留身奏事如初，知上意確不移，乃出文字乞決和議，勿許群臣預。

translations.literal: Hui again remained to memorialize as before. Knowing the emperor's intent was firmly unchanging, he then produced a written request to decide the peace talks and not permit the multitude of officials to participate.
translations.idiomatic: Hui again remained to memorialize as before; knowing the emperor's intent was firmly set, he then produced a written request to decide the peace talks and exclude other officials from participation.

sentences.zh: 鼎力求去位，以少傅出知紹興府。

translations.literal: Ding strongly sought to leave office and went out as Junior Tutor to serve as Prefect of Shaoxing.
translations.idiomatic: Ding strongly sought to leave office and departed as Junior Tutor to serve as Prefect of Shaoxing.

sentences.zh: 初，帝無子。

translations.literal: At the beginning the emperor had no son.
translations.idiomatic: At first the emperor had no son.

sentences.zh: 建炎末，范宗尹造膝有請，遂命宗室令懬擇藝祖後，得伯琮、伯玖入宮，皆藝祖七世孫。

translations.literal: At the end of the Jianyan era Fan Zongyin made a private request at the emperor's knee. The emperor then ordered clansman Ling Huan to select descendants of Emperor Taizu and brought in Bozong and Bojiu to the palace—both seventh-generation descendants of Taizu.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Jianyan era Fan Zongyin made a private request; the emperor then ordered clansman Ling Huan to select descendants of Emperor Taizu and brought Bozong and Bojiu into the palace—both seventh-generation descendants of Taizu.

sentences.zh: 伯琮改名瑗，伯玖改名璩。

translations.literal: Bozong was renamed Yuan, and Bojiu was renamed Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Bozong was renamed Yuan, and Bojiu was renamed Yu.

sentences.zh: 瑗先建節，封建國公。

translations.literal: Yuan first received a military commission and was enfeoffed as Duke of Jianguo.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan first received a military commission and was enfeoffed as Duke of Jianguo.

sentences.zh: 帝諭鼎專任其事。

translations.literal: The emperor instructed Ding to take sole charge of the matter.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor instructed Ding to take sole charge of the matter.

sentences.zh: 又請建資善堂，鼎罷，言者攻鼎，必以資善為口實。

translations.literal: He also requested establishing the Hall of Nurturing Virtue. After Ding was dismissed, critics attacked Ding and always used the Hall of Nurturing Virtue as a pretext.
translations.idiomatic: He also requested establishing the Hall of Nurturing Virtue; after Ding was dismissed, critics attacked him and always used the Hall of Nurturing Virtue as a pretext.

sentences.zh: 及鼎、檜再相，帝出禦劄，除璩節度使，封吳國公。

translations.literal: When Ding and Hui became chief ministers again, the emperor issued an imperial note appointing Yu as military commissioner and enfeoffing him as Duke of Wu.
translations.idiomatic: When Ding and Hui returned as chief ministers, the emperor issued an imperial note appointing Yu as military commissioner and enfeoffing him as Duke of Wu.

sentences.zh: 執政聚議，樞密副使王庶見之，大呼曰：「並後匹嫡，此不可行。」

translations.literal: The chief ministers gathered to deliberate. Vice Commissioner of Military Affairs Wang Shu saw it and cried out: "To set a consort equal to the principal wife—this cannot be done."
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers gathered to deliberate; Vice Commissioner of Military Affairs Wang Shu saw the note and cried out, "To set a consort equal to the principal heir—this cannot be done."

sentences.zh: 鼎以問檜，不答。

translations.literal: Ding asked Hui about it. Hui did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: Ding asked Hui about it; Hui did not answer.

sentences.zh: 檜更問鼎，鼎曰：「自丙辰罷相，議者專以此藉口，今當避嫌。」

translations.literal: Hui in turn asked Ding. Ding said: "Since I was dismissed as chief minister in the bingchen year, critics have always used this as a pretext. Now we should avoid suspicion."
translations.idiomatic: Hui in turn asked Ding; Ding said, "Since I was dismissed as chief minister in the bingchen year, critics have always used this as a pretext—we should avoid suspicion now."

sentences.zh: 約同奏面納御筆，及至帝前，檜無一語。

translations.literal: They agreed to memorialize together and return the imperial note in person, but when they came before the emperor Hui said not a word.
translations.idiomatic: They agreed to memorialize together and return the imperial note in person, but when they came before the emperor Hui said not a word.

sentences.zh: 鼎曰：「今建國在上，名雖未正，天下之人知陛下有子矣。

translations.literal: Ding said: "Now the Duke of Jianguo stands above. Though his title is not yet formalized, people throughout the realm know Your Majesty has a son.
translations.idiomatic: Ding said, "The Duke of Jianguo now stands above; though his title is not yet formalized, people throughout the realm know Your Majesty has a son.

sentences.zh: 今日禮數不得不異。」

translations.literal: Today's ceremonial treatment cannot but be different."
translations.idiomatic: Today's ceremonial treatment cannot but be different."

sentences.zh: 帝乃留御筆俟議。

translations.literal: The emperor then retained the imperial note pending deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then retained the imperial note pending deliberation.

sentences.zh: 明日，檜留身奏事。

translations.literal: The next day Hui remained to memorialize.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Hui remained to memorialize privately.

sentences.zh: 後數日，參知政事劉大中參告，亦以此為言。

translations.literal: Several days later Vice Director Liu Dazhong reported at court and also spoke on this matter.
translations.idiomatic: Several days later Vice Director Liu Dazhong reported at court and spoke on the same matter.

sentences.zh: 故鼎與大中俱罷。

translations.literal: Therefore both Ding and Dazhong were dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore both Ding and Dazhong were dismissed.

sentences.zh: 明年，璩卒授保大軍節度使，封崇國公。

translations.literal: The next year Yu was finally appointed Military Commissioner of Baoda and enfeoffed as Duke of Chongguo.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Yu was finally appointed Military Commissioner of Baoda and enfeoffed as Duke of Chongguo.

sentences.zh: 故鼎入辭，勸帝曰：「臣去後，必有以孝弟之說脅制陛下者。」

translations.literal: When Ding entered to take leave, he admonished the emperor: "After I depart, there will surely be those who use arguments of filial piety and brotherhood to coerce Your Majesty."
translations.idiomatic: When Ding entered to take leave, he admonished the emperor, "After I depart, there will surely be those who use arguments of filial piety and brotherhood to coerce Your Majesty."
