translations.idiomatic: In the third month Hui's grandson Kun, Huaiwen Pavilion Attendant-Drafter, took the jinshi examination and ranked first in both the provincial and palace examinations; Hui's nephews Chun and Yu, his affinal kin Zhou Yin, and Shen Xingjie all passed the top tier—scholar-official opinion was aggrieved.

sentences.zh: 考官則魏師遜、湯思退、鄭仲熊、沈虛中、董德元也。

translations.literal: The examiners were Wei Shixun, Tang Situi, Zheng Zhongxiong, Shen Xuzhong, and Dong Deyuan.
translations.idiomatic: The examiners were Wei Shixun, Tang Situi, Zheng Zhongxiong, Shen Xuzhong, and Dong Deyuan.

sentences.zh: 師遜等初知貢舉，即語人曰：「吾曹可以富貴矣。」

translations.literal: When Shixun and the others first learned they would oversee the examinations, they told people: "We can become rich and noble now."
translations.idiomatic: When Shixun and the others first learned they would oversee the examinations, they told people, "We can become rich and noble now."

sentences.zh: 及廷試，檜又奏思退為編排，師遜為詳定。

translations.literal: At the palace examination Hui again memorialized to appoint Situi as compiler and Shixun as final adjudicator.
translations.idiomatic: At the palace examination Hui again memorialized to appoint Situi as compiler and Shixun as final adjudicator.

sentences.zh: 塤與第二人曹冠策皆攻專門之學，張孝祥策則主一德元老且及存趙事。

translations.literal: Kun and the second-place candidate Cao Guan both attacked specialized learning in their policy essays. Zhang Xiaoxiang's essay upheld the single virtue of the elder statesman and also touched on preserving the Zhao house.
translations.idiomatic: Kun and second-place candidate Cao Guan both attacked specialized learning in their policy essays; Zhang Xiaoxiang's essay upheld the single virtue of the elder statesman and also touched on preserving the Zhao house.

sentences.zh: 帝讀塤策，皆檜、熺語，於是擢孝祥為第一，降塤第三。

translations.literal: The emperor read Kun's essay—all the words of Hui and Xi. Thereupon Xiaoxiang was raised to first place and Kun lowered to third.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor read Kun's essay—all the words of Hui and Xi; thereupon Xiaoxiang was raised to first place and Kun lowered to third.

sentences.zh: 未幾，塤修撰實錄院，宰相子孫同領史職，前所無也。

translations.literal: Before long Kun was made compiler in the Veritable Records Academy. A chief minister's descendants jointly holding historiography posts was unprecedented.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Kun was made compiler in the Veritable Records Academy—a chief minister's descendants jointly holding historiography posts was unprecedented.

sentences.zh: 六月，以王循友前知建康嘗罪檜族党，循友安置藤州。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, because Wang Xunyou, former Prefect of Jiankang, had once punished members of Hui's faction, Xunyou was assigned to Tengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, because Wang Xunyou, former Prefect of Jiankang, had once punished members of Hui's faction, Xunyou was assigned to Tengzhou.

sentences.zh: 八月，王趯為李光求內徙，趯編管辰州。

translations.literal: In the eighth month Wang Yue requested internal transfer for Li Guang. Yue was assigned to supervised exile at Chenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Wang Yue requested internal transfer for Li Guang; Yue was assigned to supervised exile at Chenzhou.

sentences.zh: 鄭玘、賈子展以會中有嘲謔講和之語，玘竄容州，子展竄德慶府。

translations.literal: Zheng Qi and Jia Zizhan, because at a gathering there were mocking words about peace talks, were exiled—Qi to Rongzhou and Zizhan to Deqing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Qi and Jia Zizhan, because at a gathering there were mocking words about peace talks, were exiled—Qi to Rongzhou and Zizhan to Deqing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 方疇以與胡銓通書，編置永州。

translations.literal: Fang Chou, for corresponding with Hu Quan, was assigned to supervised exile at Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Chou, for corresponding with Hu Quan, was assigned to supervised exile at Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 十二月，魏安行、洪興祖以廣傳程瑀《論語解》，安行編置欽州，興祖編置昭州。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month Wei Anxing and Hong Xingzu, for widely circulating Cheng Yu's Commentary on the Analects, were assigned to supervised exile—Anxing to Qinzhou and Xingzu to Chaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Wei Anxing and Hong Xingzu, for widely circulating Cheng Yu's Commentary on the Analects, were assigned to supervised exile—Anxing to Qinzhou and Xingzu to Chaozhou.

sentences.zh: 又竄程緯，以其慢上無禮也。

translations.literal: Cheng Wei was also exiled for disrespect toward superiors and lack of propriety.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Wei was also exiled for disrespect toward superiors and lack of propriety.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗諭檜曰：「近輪對者，多謁告避免。

translations.literal: The emperor once instructed Hui: "Recently those taking turns at audience mostly request leave to avoid it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once instructed Hui, "Recently those taking turns at audience mostly request leave to avoid it.

sentences.zh: 百官輪對，正欲聞所未聞，可令檢舉約束。」

translations.literal: Officials taking turns at audience is precisely to hear what has not been heard. You may order investigation and restraint."
translations.idiomatic: Officials taking turns at audience is precisely to hear what has not been heard—you may order investigation and restraint."

sentences.zh: 檜擅政以來，屏塞人言，蔽上耳目，凡一時獻言者，非誦檜功德，則訐人語言以中傷善類。

translations.literal: Since Hui monopolized government, he blocked human speech and covered the emperor's ears and eyes. All who offered opinions at the time either recited Hui's merit and virtue or picked at people's words to harm the good.
translations.idiomatic: Since Hui monopolized government, he blocked human speech and covered the emperor's ears and eyes—all who offered opinions either recited Hui's merit and virtue or picked at people's words to harm the good.

sentences.zh: 欲有言者恐觸忌諱，畏言國事，僅論銷金鋪翠、乞禁鹿胎冠子之類，以塞責而已。

translations.literal: Those who wished to speak feared touching taboos and dreaded speaking on state affairs, discussing only such things as gilding and inlaying jade or requesting bans on deer-fetus caps—merely to fulfill obligation.
translations.idiomatic: Those who wished to speak feared touching taboos and dreaded speaking on state affairs, discussing only such things as gilding and inlaying jade or requesting bans on deer-fetus caps—merely to fulfill obligation.

sentences.zh: 故帝及之，蓋亦防檜之壅蔽也。

translations.literal: Therefore the emperor brought this up—likely also to guard against Hui's obstruction and concealment.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the emperor brought this up—likely also to guard against Hui's obstruction and concealment.

sentences.zh: 衢州嘗有盜起，檜遣殿前司將官辛立將千人捕之，不以聞。

translations.literal: Once when bandits rose in Quzhou, Hui sent Palace Guard general Xin Li with a thousand men to capture them and did not report it.
translations.idiomatic: Once when bandits rose in Quzhou, Hui sent Palace Guard general Xin Li with a thousand men to capture them and did not report it.

sentences.zh: 晉安郡王因入侍言之，帝大驚，問檜，檜曰：「不足上煩聖慮，故不敢聞，盜平即奏矣。」

translations.literal: The Prince of Jin'an mentioned it while attending the emperor. The emperor was greatly alarmed and asked Hui. Hui said: "It was not worth troubling Your Majesty's concern, so I dared not report it. Once the bandits were pacified I would memorialize."
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Jin'an mentioned it while attending the emperor; the emperor was greatly alarmed and asked Hui, who said, "It was not worth troubling Your Majesty's concern, so I dared not report it—once the bandits were pacified I would memorialize."

sentences.zh: 退而求其故，知晉安言之，遂奏晉安居秀王喪不當給俸，月損二百緡，帝為出內帑給之。

translations.literal: On withdrawing he sought the reason and learned the Prince of Jin'an had spoken. He memorialized that the Prince, residing in the Xiuwang residence during mourning, should not receive salary, reducing him by two hundred strings of cash per month. The emperor provided it from the inner treasury.
translations.idiomatic: On withdrawing he sought the reason and learned the Prince of Jin'an had spoken; he memorialized that the Prince, residing in the Xiuwang residence during mourning, should not receive salary, reducing him by two hundred strings of cash per month—the emperor provided it from the inner treasury.

sentences.zh: 二十五年二月，以沈長卿舊與李光啟譏和議，又與芮燁共賦《牡丹詩》，有「寧令漢社稷，變作莽乾坤」之句，為鄰人所告，長卿編置化州，燁武岡軍。

translations.literal: In the second month of the twenty-fifth year, because Shen Changqing had formerly joined Li Guang in mocking peace talks and also composed Peony Poems with Rui Ye containing the line "Better let Han's altars of state change into Mang's cosmos," he was reported by a neighbor. Changqing was assigned to supervised exile at Huazhou and Ye to Wugang Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the twenty-fifth year, because Shen Changqing had formerly joined Li Guang in mocking peace talks and also composed Peony Poems with Rui Ye containing the line "Better let Han's altars of state change into Mang's cosmos," he was reported by a neighbor—Changqing was assigned to supervised exile at Huazhou and Ye to Wugang Army.

sentences.zh: 靜江有驛名秦城，知府呂願中率賓僚共賦《秦城王氣詩》以媚檜，不賦者劉芮、李燮、羅博文三人而已。

translations.literal: In Jingjiang there was a post station named Qin City. Prefect Lü Yuanzhong led his guests and subordinates to compose together Qin City Royal Qi Poems to flatter Hui. Only Liu Rui, Li Xie, and Luo Bowen did not compose.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingjiang there was a post station named Qin City; Prefect Lü Yuanzhong led his guests and subordinates to compose Qin City Royal Qi Poems to flatter Hui—only Liu Rui, Li Xie, and Luo Bowen did not compose.

sentences.zh: 願中由此得召。

translations.literal: Yuanzhong was thereby summoned to court.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhong was thereby summoned to court.

sentences.zh: 又張扶請檜乘金根車，又有乞置益國官屬及議九錫者，檜聞之安然。

translations.literal: Zhang Fu also requested that Hui ride the golden-root carriage, and there were also those who asked to establish Yiguo official staff and discussed the nine bestowals. Hui heard it all calmly.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Fu also requested that Hui ride the golden-root carriage, and there were also those who asked to establish Yiguo official staff and discussed the nine bestowals—Hui heard it all calmly.

sentences.zh: 十月，申禁專門之學。

translations.literal: In the tenth month specialized learning was again banned.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month specialized learning was again banned.

sentences.zh: 以太廟靈芝繪為華旗，凡郡國所奏瑞木、嘉禾、瑞瓜、雙蓮悉繪之。

translations.literal: The imperial temple's auspicious fungus was painted as a splendid banner, and all auspicious trees, fine grain, auspicious melons, and twin lotuses memorialized by prefectures and commanderies were painted as well.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial temple's auspicious fungus was painted as a splendid banner, and all auspicious trees, fine grain, auspicious melons, and twin lotuses memorialized by prefectures and commanderies were painted as well.

sentences.zh: 趙令衿觀檜《家廟記》，口誦「君子之澤，五世而斬」，為汪召錫所告。

translations.literal: Zhao Lingqin, reading Hui's Record of the Family Temple, recited aloud "A gentleman's influence fades by the fifth generation." He was reported by Wang Zhaoxi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Lingqin, reading Hui's Record of the Family Temple, recited aloud "A gentleman's influence fades by the fifth generation"—he was reported by Wang Zhaoxi.

sentences.zh: 御史徐𡕇又論趙鼎子汾與令衿飲別厚贐，必有奸謀，詔送大理，拘令衿南外宗正司。

translations.literal: Censor Xu Kan further argued that Zhao Ding's son Fen and Lingqin, drinking farewell with generous parting gifts, must have had treacherous designs. An edict ordered them sent to the Court of Judicial Review and Lingqin detained at the Southern Outer Imperial Clan Office.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Xu Kan further argued that Zhao Ding's son Fen and Lingqin, drinking farewell with generous parting gifts, must have had treacherous designs; an edict ordered them sent to the Court of Judicial Review and Lingqin detained at the Southern Outer Imperial Clan Office.

sentences.zh: 檜於一德格天閣書趙鼎、李光、胡銓姓名，必欲殺之而後已。

translations.literal: In the Single Virtue Matches Heaven Hall Hui wrote the names of Zhao Ding, Li Guang, and Hu Quan. He was determined not to stop until he had killed them.
translations.idiomatic: In the Single Virtue Matches Heaven Hall Hui wrote the names of Zhao Ding, Li Guang, and Hu Quan—he was determined not to stop until he had killed them.

sentences.zh: 鼎已死而憾之不置，遂欲孥戮汾。

translations.literal: Ding was already dead yet Hui's resentment did not cease, and he then wished to execute Fen and his family.
translations.idiomatic: Ding was already dead yet Hui's resentment did not cease, and he then wished to execute Fen and his family.

sentences.zh: 檜忌張浚尤甚，故令衿之獄，張宗元之罷，皆波及浚。

translations.literal: Hui especially envied Zhang Jun. Therefore the case of Lingqin and the dismissal of Zhang Zongyuan both implicated Jun.
translations.idiomatic: Hui especially envied Zhang Jun; therefore the case of Lingqin and the dismissal of Zhang Zongyuan both implicated Jun.

sentences.zh: 浚在永州，檜又使其死黨張柄知潭州，與郡丞汪召錫共伺察之。

translations.literal: Jun was at Yongzhou. Hui again had his dead-partisan Zhang Bing made Prefect of Tanzhou to watch him together with Vice Prefect Wang Zhaoxi.
translations.idiomatic: Jun was at Yongzhou; Hui again had his partisan Zhang Bing made Prefect of Tanzhou to watch him together with Vice Prefect Wang Zhaoxi.

sentences.zh: 至是，使汾自誣與浚及李光、胡寅謀大逆，凡一時賢士五十三人皆與焉。

translations.literal: By this time he had Fen falsely accuse himself of plotting great treason with Jun, Li Guang, and Hu Yin. In all, fifty-three worthy men of the time were implicated.
translations.idiomatic: By this time he had Fen falsely accuse himself of plotting great treason with Jun, Li Guang, and Hu Yin—in all, fifty-three worthy men of the time were implicated.

sentences.zh: 獄成，而檜病不能書。

translations.literal: The case was concluded, but Hui was ill and could not write.
translations.idiomatic: The case was concluded, but Hui was ill and could not write.

sentences.zh: 是月乙未，帝幸檜第問疾，檜無一語，惟流涕而已。

translations.literal: On the yimwei day of that month the emperor visited Hui's residence to inquire after his illness. Hui said not a word and only wept.
translations.idiomatic: On the yimwei day of that month the emperor visited Hui's residence to inquire after his illness; Hui said not a word and only wept.

sentences.zh: 熺奏請代居相位者，帝曰：「此事卿不當與。」

translations.literal: Xi memorialized asking who would replace him in the chief ministership. The emperor said: "In this matter you should not participate."
translations.idiomatic: Xi memorialized asking who would replace him in the chief ministership; the emperor said, "In this matter you should not participate."

sentences.zh: 帝遂命權直學士院沈虛中草檜父子致仕制。

translations.literal: The emperor then ordered Acting Direct Academician Shen Xuzhong to draft the retirement edicts for Hui and his son.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then ordered Acting Direct Academician Shen Xuzhong to draft the retirement edicts for Hui and his son.

sentences.zh: 熺猶遣其子塤與林一飛、鄭柟夜見台諫徐喜、張扶謀奏請己為相。

translations.literal: Xi still sent his son Kun with Lin Yifei and Zheng Nan to see censors and remonstrators Xu Xi and Zhang Fu by night, plotting to memorialize requesting himself as chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: Xi still sent his son Kun with Lin Yifei and Zheng Nan to see censors and remonstrators Xu Xi and Zhang Fu by night, plotting to memorialize requesting himself as chief minister.

sentences.zh: 丙申，詔檜加封建康郡王，熺進少師，皆致仕，塤、堪並提舉江州太平興國宮。

translations.literal: On the bingshen day an edict advanced Hui to Prince of Jiankang Commandery and Xi to Junior Preceptor; both retired from office. Kun and Kan were both made directors of the Taiping Xingguo Palace in Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On the bingshen day an edict advanced Hui to Prince of Jiankang Commandery and Xi to Junior Preceptor; both retired from office—Kun and Kan were both made directors of the Taiping Xingguo Palace in Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 是夜，檜卒，年六十六。

translations.literal: That night Hui died, aged sixty-six.
translations.idiomatic: That night Hui died, aged sixty-six.

sentences.zh: 後贈申王，諡忠獻。

translations.literal: Later he was posthumously made Prince of Shen and given the posthumous title Zhongxian.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was posthumously made Prince of Shen and given the posthumous title Zhongxian, "Loyal and Dedicated."

sentences.zh: 檜兩據相位者，凡十九年，劫制君父，包藏禍心，倡和誤國，忘仇斁倫。

translations.literal: Hui twice held the chief ministership for nineteen years in all—coercing ruler and father, harboring treacherous intent, advocating peace to ruin the state, forgetting enmity and violating human relations.
translations.idiomatic: Hui twice held the chief ministership for nineteen years in all—coercing ruler and father, harboring treacherous intent, advocating peace to ruin the state, forgetting enmity and violating human relations.

sentences.zh: 一時忠臣良將，誅鋤略盡。

translations.literal: The loyal ministers and worthy generals of the time were executed and eliminated nearly to the last.
translations.idiomatic: The loyal ministers and worthy generals of the time were executed and eliminated nearly to the last.

sentences.zh: 其頑鈍無恥者，率為檜用，爭以誣陷善類為功。

translations.literal: Those who were stubborn, dull, and shameless were mostly used by Hui, competing to make falsely accusing the good their achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Those who were stubborn, dull, and shameless were mostly used by Hui, competing to make falsely accusing the good their achievement.

sentences.zh: 其矯誣也，無罪可狀，不過曰謗訕，曰指斥，曰怨望，曰立黨沽名，甚則曰有無君心。

translations.literal: In their fabrications, when no crime could be described, they said only slander, pointing and reproach, resentment and longing, forming factions to seek fame—and in extreme cases, having a heart without a ruler.
translations.idiomatic: In their fabrications, when no crime could be described, they said only slander, pointing and reproach, resentment and longing, forming factions to seek fame—and in extreme cases, having a heart without a ruler.

sentences.zh: 凡論人章疏，皆檜自操以授言者，識之者曰：「此老秦筆也。」

translations.literal: All memorials discussing people were written by Hui himself and given to those who spoke. Those who recognized them said: "This is Old Qin's brush."
translations.idiomatic: All memorials discussing people were written by Hui himself and given to those who spoke; those who recognized them said, "This is Old Qin's brush."

sentences.zh: 察事之卒，佈滿京城，小涉譏議，即捕治，中以深文。

translations.literal: Spies were spread throughout the capital. The slightest involvement in mockery or criticism meant immediate arrest and punishment, applied with harsh legal interpretation.
translations.idiomatic: Spies were spread throughout the capital—the slightest involvement in mockery or criticism meant immediate arrest and punishment, applied with harsh legal interpretation.

sentences.zh: 又陰結內侍及醫師王繼先，伺上動靜。

translations.literal: He also secretly connected with eunuchs and the physician Wang Jixian to watch the emperor's movements.
translations.idiomatic: He also secretly connected with eunuchs and the physician Wang Jixian to watch the emperor's movements.

sentences.zh: 郡國事惟申省，無一至上前者。

translations.literal: Affairs of commanderies and kingdoms were reported only to the provinces; not one reached the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Affairs of commanderies and kingdoms were reported only to the provinces—not one reached the throne.

sentences.zh: 檜死，帝方與人言之。

translations.literal: After Hui died, the emperor spoke of it with others for the first time.
translations.idiomatic: Only after Hui died did the emperor speak of it with others.

sentences.zh: 檜立久任之說，士淹滯失職，有十年不解者。

translations.literal: Hui established the doctrine of long tenure. Scholars stagnated and lost office; some went ten years without release.
translations.idiomatic: Hui established the doctrine of long tenure; scholars stagnated and lost office, some going ten years without release.

sentences.zh: 附己者立與擢用。

translations.literal: Those who attached themselves to him were immediately promoted and employed.
translations.idiomatic: Those who attached themselves to him were immediately promoted and employed.

sentences.zh: 自其獨相，至死之日，易執政二十八人，皆世無一譽。

translations.literal: From the time he held the chief ministership alone until the day he died, twenty-eight men held executive power in succession, and the world had not a word of praise for any of them.
translations.idiomatic: From the time he held the chief ministership alone until the day he died, twenty-eight men held executive power in succession—and the world had not a word of praise for any of them.

sentences.zh: 柔佞易制者，如孫近、韓肖胄、樓炤、王次翁、范同、万俟禼、程克俊、李文會、楊願、李若谷、何若、段拂、汪勃、詹大方、餘堯弼、巫伋、章夏、宋朴、史才、魏師遜、施钜、鄭仲熊之徒，率拔之冗散，遽躋政地。

translations.literal: Those who were soft, flatteringly compliant, and easy to control—such as Sun Jin, Han Xiaozhou, Lou Zhao, Wang Ciweng, Fan Tong, Wan Qixie, Cheng Kejun, Li Wenhui, Yang Yuan, Li Ruogu, He Ruo, Duan Fu, Wang Bo, Zhan Dafang, Yu Yaobi, Wu Ji, Zhang Xia, Song Pu, Shi Cai, Wei Shixun, Shi Ju, Zheng Zhongxiong, and the like—were mostly plucked from idle and scattered posts and suddenly elevated to the seats of power.
translations.idiomatic: Those who were soft, flatteringly compliant, and easy to control—such as Sun Jin, Han Xiaozhou, Lou Zhao, Wang Ciweng, Fan Tong, Wan Qixie, Cheng Kejun, Li Wenhui, Yang Yuan, Li Ruogu, He Ruo, Duan Fu, Wang Bo, Zhan Dafang, Yu Yaobi, Wu Ji, Zhang Xia, Song Pu, Shi Cai, Wei Shixun, Shi Ju, Zheng Zhongxiong, and the like—were mostly plucked from idle posts and suddenly elevated to the seats of power.

sentences.zh: 既共政，則拱默而已。

translations.literal: Once they shared power, they merely bowed in silence.
translations.idiomatic: Once they shared power, they merely bowed in silence.

sentences.zh: 又多自言官聽檜彈擊，輒以政府報之，由中丞、諫議而升者凡十有二人，然甫入即出，或一閱月，或半年即罷去。

translations.literal: Many also declared that their offices listened to Hui's impeachments and at once reported them to the government. Those promoted from censor-in-chief and remonstrator numbered twelve in all, yet as soon as they entered they departed—some after one month, some dismissed within half a year.
translations.idiomatic: Many also declared that their offices listened to Hui's impeachments and at once reported them to the government; those promoted from censor-in-chief and remonstrator numbered twelve in all, yet as soon as they entered they departed—some after one month, some dismissed within half a year.

sentences.zh: 惟王次翁閱四年，以金人敗盟之初持不易相之論，檜德之深也。

translations.literal: Only Wang Ciweng lasted four years, because at the beginning of the Jurchen breach of treaty he held to the view that the chief minister should not be changed. Hui was deeply grateful to him.
translations.idiomatic: Only Wang Ciweng lasted four years, because at the beginning of the Jurchen breach of treaty he held that the chief minister should not be changed—Hui was deeply grateful to him.

sentences.zh: 開門受賂，富敵于國，外國珍寶，死猶及門。

translations.literal: He opened his door to receive bribes; his wealth rivaled the state. Foreign treasures still reached his gate after his death.
translations.idiomatic: He opened his door to receive bribes; his wealth rivaled the state—foreign treasures still reached his gate after his death.

sentences.zh: 人謂熺自檜秉政無日不鍛酒具，治書畫，特其細爾。

translations.literal: People said that from the day Hui held power Xi never passed a day without forging wine vessels and tending calligraphy and painting—but these were only the small matters.
translations.idiomatic: People said that from the day Hui held power Xi never passed a day without forging wine vessels and tending calligraphy and painting—but these were only the small matters.

sentences.zh: 檜陰險如崖阱，深阻竟叵測。

translations.literal: Hui was treacherous as a cliff trap; his depths and barriers were ultimately unfathomable.
translations.idiomatic: Hui was treacherous as a cliff trap—his depths and barriers were ultimately unfathomable.

sentences.zh: 同列論事上前，未嘗力辨，但以一二語傾擠之。

translations.literal: When colleagues deliberated on affairs before the emperor, he never argued forcefully but used only a word or two to topple and squeeze them out.
translations.idiomatic: When colleagues deliberated on affairs before the emperor, he never argued forcefully but used only a word or two to topple and squeeze them out.

sentences.zh: 李光嘗與檜爭論，言頗侵檜，檜不答。

translations.literal: Li Guang once argued with Hui, his words quite encroaching on Hui. Hui did not reply.
translations.idiomatic: Li Guang once argued with Hui, his words quite encroaching on Hui—Hui did not reply.

sentences.zh: 及光言畢，檜徐曰：「李光無人臣禮。」

translations.literal: When Guang had finished speaking, Hui said slowly: "Li Guang lacks the propriety of a minister."
translations.idiomatic: When Guang had finished speaking, Hui said slowly, "Li Guang lacks the propriety of a minister."

sentences.zh: 帝始怒之。

translations.literal: The emperor then grew angry at Guang.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then grew angry at Guang.

sentences.zh: 凡陷忠良，率用此術。

translations.literal: In all cases of entrapping the loyal and worthy, he generally used this technique.
translations.idiomatic: In entrapping the loyal and worthy, he generally used this technique.

sentences.zh: 晚年殘忍尤甚，數興大獄，而又喜諛佞，不避形跡。

translations.literal: In his later years he was especially cruel, repeatedly opening great cases, and also delighted in flattery and sycophancy without avoiding visible traces.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years he was especially cruel, repeatedly opening great cases, and also delighted in flattery and sycophancy without concealing it.

sentences.zh: 然檜死熺廢，其党祖述餘說，力持和議，以竊據相位者尚數人，至孝宗始蕩滌無餘。

translations.literal: Yet after Hui died and Xi was discarded, his faction inherited and propagated his remaining doctrines, forcefully upheld peace talks, and several men still usurped the chief ministership by stealth—not until Emperor Xiaozong were they swept away without remainder.
translations.idiomatic: Yet after Hui died and Xi was discarded, his faction inherited and propagated his remaining doctrines, forcefully upheld peace talks, and several men still usurped the chief ministership—not until Emperor Xiaozong were they swept away without remainder.

sentences.zh: 開禧二年四月，追奪王爵，改諡謬醜。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the second year of Kaixi his princely rank was posthumously revoked and his posthumous title changed to Miaochou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the second year of Kaixi his princely rank was posthumously revoked and his posthumous title changed to Miaochou, "Deceitful and Ugly."

sentences.zh: 嘉定元年，史彌遠奏復王爵、贈諡。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jiading Shi Miyuan memorialized to restore his princely rank and grant a posthumous title.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jiading Shi Miyuan memorialized to restore his princely rank and grant a posthumous title.
